# pdfmake documentation

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/

Build a PDF in three steps: configure the runtime, describe the content, then request an output.

## 1. Choose your runtime




Use Node.js 20 or later. Install the pinned version below, save the complete example as `first-pdf.cjs`, then run `node first-pdf.cjs`.

```sh
npm install pdfmake@0.3.12
```

**JavaScript**

```js
const pdfmake = require('pdfmake');

const fonts = require('pdfmake/standard-fonts/Helvetica');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
const standardNames = new Set(Object.values(fonts.Helvetica));
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(name => standardNames.has(name));

async function main() {
  const definition = {
    defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' },
    content: [
      { text: 'Hello, pdfmake!', fontSize: 24, bold: true },
      'Your first PDF, generated in Node.js.'
    ]
  };
  await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).write('document.pdf');
}

main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";
import pdfmake from "pdfmake";

const fonts = require('pdfmake/standard-fonts/Helvetica');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
const standardNames = new Set(Object.values(fonts.Helvetica));
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(name => standardNames.has(name));

async function main() {
  const definition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' },
    content: [
      { text: 'Hello, pdfmake!', fontSize: 24, bold: true },
      'Your first PDF, generated in Node.js.'
    ]
  };
  await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).write('document.pdf');
}

main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
```

[Node.js quickstart](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/)




The browser needs the engine and fonts, loaded in that order. The complete quickstart includes a download button and error handling.

[Browser quickstart](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/)



## 2. Understand the definition

A definition is a JavaScript object, not HTML. `content` lists blocks in reading order. This example generates exactly the PDF shown. Open it in the playground to edit it, then return here without losing your workspace.



### Runnable example: 01 · First document

**JavaScript**

```js
// Define a fresh document in dd. Ctrl/⌘ + Enter to run.
var dd = {
  content: [
    { text: 'Make something clear.', fontSize: 30, bold: true, color: '#08786b', margin: [0, 0, 0, 16] },
    'A paragraph, a table, a report. Start here and make it yours.',
    { text: 'Built with pdfmake', italics: true, color: '#667d73', margin: [0, 20, 0, 0] }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

// Define a fresh document in dd. Ctrl/⌘ + Enter to run.
var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    { text: 'Make something clear.', fontSize: 30, bold: true, color: '#08786b', margin: [0, 0, 0, 16] },
    'A paragraph, a table, a report. Start here and make it yours.',
    { text: 'Built with pdfmake', italics: true, color: '#667d73', margin: [0, 20, 0, 0] }
  ]
};
```

[See the rendered PDF and edit this example](https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/playground/?example=welcome)



## 3. Continue with the right building block

- [Your first PDF](/docs/0.3/learn/first-pdf/)
- [The document model](/docs/0.3/learn/document-model/)
- [Styling](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/styling/)
- [Tables](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/tables/)
- [Fonts and character coverage](/docs/0.3/fonts/)
- [Errors and diagnostics](/docs/0.3/guides/errors/)

Use a fresh definition for every generation; layout mutates the object. Output methods return Promises: await them and handle failures.

# Document definition reference

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/

## Shape of a definition

**JavaScript**

```js
const docDefinition = {
  pageSize: 'A4',
  pageOrientation: 'portrait',
  pageMargins: [40, 50, 40, 50],
  defaultStyle: { fontSize: 12 },
  styles: { heading: { fontSize: 20, bold: true } },
  info: { title: 'Example document', author: 'Example author' },
  content: [
    { text: 'Document heading', style: 'heading' },
    'A plain string becomes a paragraph.',
    { ul: ['First item', 'Second item'] }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

const docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  pageSize: 'A4',
  pageOrientation: 'portrait',
  pageMargins: [40, 50, 40, 50],
  defaultStyle: { fontSize: 12 },
  styles: { heading: { fontSize: 20, bold: true } },
  info: { title: 'Example document', author: 'Example author' },
  content: [
    { text: 'Document heading', style: 'heading' },
    'A plain string becomes a paragraph.',
    { ul: ['First item', 'Second item'] }
  ]
};
```

Pass the definition to your runtime's `createPdf` method after configuring fonts. All numeric dimensions use **points** (72 points per inch). Margins use the order **left, top, right, bottom**. A content array is a vertical stack. Create a fresh object for each render; the layout process adds internal measurements and positions.

## Content nodes

| Node | Purpose | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `{ text: '...' }` | Paragraph or inline runs | [Styling](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/styling/) |
| `{ stack: [...] }` | Group blocks and apply a shared style | [Stacks](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/stack/) |
| `{ columns: [...] }` | Side-by-side content | [Columns](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/columns/) |
| `{ table: { body: [...] } }` | Rows, cells and repeating headers | [Tables](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/tables/) |
| `{ ul: [...] }`, `{ ol: [...] }` | Bullet and numbered lists | [Lists](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/lists/) |
| `{ image: 'key' }` | PNG or JPEG | [Images](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/images/) |
| `{ svg: '<svg>...</svg>' }` | SVG vector content | [SVGs](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/svgs/) |
| `{ qr: '...' }` | QR code | [QR](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/qr/) |

## Document-level settings

- [Page size, orientation and breaks](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/page/), [margins](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/margins/) and [sections](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/sections/).
- [Headers and footers](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/headers-footers/), [backgrounds](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/background-layer/) and [watermarks](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/watermark/).
- [Metadata](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/document-medatadata/), [links](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/links/), [table of contents](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/toc/) and [outlines](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/outlines/).
- [Attachments](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/attachments/), [encryption](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/security/), [PDF/A](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/pdfa/) and [compression](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/compression/).

## Definition versus rendering options

Content and visual settings belong in the definition. `fontLayoutCache` and `bufferPages` belong in the second `createPdf` argument. Fonts, table layout registrations and resource policies belong on the pdfmake API. See [API reference](/docs/0.3/guides/api-reference/).

---

# Attachments embedding

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/attachments/

pdfmake supports attaching files as annotations as well as embedded files.
Embedded files are added in the "files" dictionary and will show up in supported pdf viewers in their respective attachment panels.
File attachments are annotations which link to a file.
Any attachment or embedded file must provide at least a "src", providing a filename through "name" is highly recommended.
The "src" of any attachment can be provided in dataURL format (like the following attachment, taken from http://www.clipartbest.com/clipart-dT7zx5rT9), but local files are allowed as well.

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
	content: [
		'Any attachment or embedded file must provide at least a "src", providing a filename through "name" is highly recommended.',
		'The "src" of any attachment can be provided in dataURL format (like the following attachment, taken from http://www.clipartbest.com/clipart-dT7zx5rT9), but local files are allowed as well.',
		{
			attachment: {
				src: 'data:image/png;base64,iVBOR....',
				name: 'testImage.png'
			}
		},
		'You can also define an attachment in the "attachments" dictionary and reference it by name.',
		{
			attachment: 'sampleImage'
		},
		'And there are three different standard icons for attachments, "GraphPush", "Paperclip", and "Push" (the default value). Set them with the "icon" option.',
		{
			attachment: 'sampleImage',
			icon: 'GraphPush'
		},
		{
			attachment: 'sampleImage',
			icon: 'Paperclip'
		},
		{
			attachment: 'sampleImage',
			icon: 'Push'
		},
		'For better customization, add an image and attach a file to it with linkToFile:',
		{
			image: 'fonts/sampleImage.jpg',
			width: 150,
			linkToFile: 'sampleImage'
		},
		"You can add a description, which will show in your pdf viewer's attachments panel and as a tooltip when hovering over the attachment.",
		{
			attachment: {
				src: 'data:image/png;base64,iVBOR....',
				name: 'withDescription.png',
				description: 'file description'
			}
		},
		'You can also define the "src" of an attachment or embedded file in the "attachments" and "files" dictionary via URL address.',
	],
	attachments: {
		sampleImage: {
			src: 'fonts/sampleImage.jpg',
			name: 'sampleImage.png'
		}
	},
	files: {
		README: {
			src: 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bpampuch/pdfmake/master/README.md',
			name: 'pdfmake README.md'
		}
	}
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
	content: [
		'Any attachment or embedded file must provide at least a "src", providing a filename through "name" is highly recommended.',
		'The "src" of any attachment can be provided in dataURL format (like the following attachment, taken from http://www.clipartbest.com/clipart-dT7zx5rT9), but local files are allowed as well.',
		{
			attachment: {
				src: 'data:image/png;base64,iVBOR....',
				name: 'testImage.png'
			}
		},
		'You can also define an attachment in the "attachments" dictionary and reference it by name.',
		{
			attachment: 'sampleImage'
		},
		'And there are three different standard icons for attachments, "GraphPush", "Paperclip", and "Push" (the default value). Set them with the "icon" option.',
		{
			attachment: 'sampleImage',
			icon: 'GraphPush'
		},
		{
			attachment: 'sampleImage',
			icon: 'Paperclip'
		},
		{
			attachment: 'sampleImage',
			icon: 'Push'
		},
		'For better customization, add an image and attach a file to it with linkToFile:',
		{
			image: 'fonts/sampleImage.jpg',
			width: 150,
			linkToFile: 'sampleImage'
		},
		"You can add a description, which will show in your pdf viewer's attachments panel and as a tooltip when hovering over the attachment.",
		{
			attachment: {
				src: 'data:image/png;base64,iVBOR....',
				name: 'withDescription.png',
				description: 'file description'
			}
		},
		'You can also define the "src" of an attachment or embedded file in the "attachments" and "files" dictionary via URL address.',
	],
	attachments: {
		sampleImage: {
			src: 'fonts/sampleImage.jpg',
			name: 'sampleImage.png'
		}
	},
	files: {
		README: {
			src: 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bpampuch/pdfmake/master/README.md',
			name: 'pdfmake README.md'
		}
	}
};
```

# Background-layer

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/background-layer/

The background-layer will be added on every page.

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  background: 'simple text',

  content: ['Example document content']
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  background: 'simple text',

  content: ['Example document content']
};
```

It may contain any other object as well (images, tables, ...) or be dynamically generated:

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  background: function(currentPage, pageSize) {
    return `page ${currentPage} with size ${pageSize.width} x ${pageSize.height}`
  },

  content: ['Example document content']
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  background: function(currentPage, pageSize) {
    return `page ${currentPage} with size ${pageSize.width} x ${pageSize.height}`
  },

  content: ['Example document content']
};
```

---

# Columns

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/columns/

By default paragraphs are rendered as a vertical stack of elements (one below another). It is possible however to divide available space into columns.

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    'This paragraph fills full width, as there are no columns. Next paragraph however consists of three columns',
    {
      columns: [
        {
          // auto-sized columns have their widths based on their content
          width: 'auto',
          text: 'First column'
        },
        {
          // star-sized columns fill the remaining space
          // if there's more than one star-column, available width is divided equally
          width: '*',
          text: 'Second column'
        },
        {
          // fixed width
          width: 100,
          text: 'Third column'
        },
        {
          // % width
          width: '20%',
          text: 'Fourth column'
        }
      ],
      // optional space between columns
      columnGap: 10
    },
    'This paragraph goes below all columns and has full width'
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    'This paragraph fills full width, as there are no columns. Next paragraph however consists of three columns',
    {
      columns: [
        {
          // auto-sized columns have their widths based on their content
          width: 'auto',
          text: 'First column'
        },
        {
          // star-sized columns fill the remaining space
          // if there's more than one star-column, available width is divided equally
          width: '*',
          text: 'Second column'
        },
        {
          // fixed width
          width: 100,
          text: 'Third column'
        },
        {
          // % width
          width: '20%',
          text: 'Fourth column'
        }
      ],
      // optional space between columns
      columnGap: 10
    },
    'This paragraph goes below all columns and has full width'
  ]
};
```

Column content is not limited to a simple text. It can actually contain any valid pdfmake element. Make sure to look at the COLUMNS example in [playground](/docs/0.3/playground/).


## Properties

* `columnGap: number` specify gap (space) between columns
* `snakingColumns: boolean` snaking columns (newspaper-style columns) see this [article](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/snaking-columns/) _(Minimal version: 0.3.5)_

---

# Compression

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/compression/

## Default behavior

PDF stream compression is enabled by default. To disable it for inspection:

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  compress: false,
  content: ['An uncompressed example document.']
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  compress: false,
  content: ['An uncompressed example document.']
};
```

`compress` is a boolean field on the document definition, not the `createPdf` options object. Disabling it generally increases output size. It does not remove font embedding or image data and is not a way to reduce layout memory. See [performance](/docs/0.3/guides/performance/) for measurement guidance.

---

# Document Metadata

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/document-medatadata/

PDF documents can have various metadata associated with them, such as the title, or author
of the document. You can add that information by adding it to the document definition

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  info: {
	title: 'awesome Document',
	author: 'john doe',
	subject: 'subject of document',
	keywords: 'keywords for document',
  },
  content:  'This is an sample PDF printed with pdfMake'
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  info: {
	title: 'awesome Document',
	author: 'john doe',
	subject: 'subject of document',
	keywords: 'keywords for document',
  },
  content:  'This is an sample PDF printed with pdfMake'
}
```

Standard properties:

* `title` - the title of the document
* `author` - the name of the author
* `subject` - the subject of the document
* `keywords` - keywords associated with the document
* `creator` - the creator of the document (default is 'pdfmake')
* `producer` - the producer of the document (default is 'pdfmake')
* `creationDate` - the date the document was created (added automatically by pdfmake)
* `modDate` - the date the document was last modified
* `trapped` - the trapped flag in a PDF document indicates whether the document has been "trapped", i.e. corrected for slight color misregistrations

Custom properties:

You can add custom properties. Key of property not contain spaces.

## Document language

PDF document can have custom language set via `language` property.

Example:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  language: 'cs-CZ',
  content: 'Jednoduchý PDF dokument vytvoření pomocí pdfmake'
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  language: 'cs-CZ',
  content: 'Jednoduchý PDF dokument vytvoření pomocí pdfmake'
}
```

---

# Headers and footers

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/headers-footers/

## Add a static header

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  pageMargins: [40, 65, 40, 55],
  header: { text: 'Example report', margin: [40, 20, 40, 0] },
  footer: { text: 'Example Studio', alignment: 'center', fontSize: 9 },
  content: ['Document content']
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  pageMargins: [40, 65, 40, 55],
  header: { text: 'Example report', margin: [40, 20, 40, 0] },
  footer: { text: 'Example Studio', alignment: 'center', fontSize: 9 },
  content: ['Document content']
};
```

Headers and footers repeat on pages. Reserve enough top and bottom margin for their contents; they do not automatically enlarge the body margins. Returned content uses normal pdfmake nodes.

## Add page numbers

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  pageMargins: [40, 65, 40, 55],
  header: function (currentPage, pageCount, pageSize) {
    return {
      text: 'Report · ' + pageSize.width + ' pt wide',
      alignment: currentPage % 2 ? 'left' : 'right',
      margin: [40, 20, 40, 0],
      fontSize: 9
    };
  },
  footer: function (currentPage, pageCount) {
    return { text: currentPage + ' of ' + pageCount, alignment: 'center', fontSize: 9 };
  },
  content: ['First page', { text: 'Second page', pageBreak: 'before' }]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  pageMargins: [40, 65, 40, 55],
  header: function (currentPage, pageCount, pageSize) {
    return {
      text: 'Report · ' + pageSize.width + ' pt wide',
      alignment: currentPage % 2 ? 'left' : 'right',
      margin: [40, 20, 40, 0],
      fontSize: 9
    };
  },
  footer: function (currentPage, pageCount) {
    return { text: currentPage + ' of ' + pageCount, alignment: 'center', fontSize: 9 };
  },
  content: ['First page', { text: 'Second page', pageBreak: 'before' }]
};
```

Callbacks receive the current page number (starting at 1), total page count and page size. Return a fresh node for each invocation. Keep callbacks deterministic and avoid modifying shared application data.

---

# Images

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/images/

## Reuse embedded PNG or JPEG data

An image node is `{ image: 'key' }`, where the key resolves through the document's
`images` dictionary. Reuse a key when the same image appears more than once.
PNG and JPEG are supported; use an [SVG node](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/svgs/)
for SVG content.



### Runnable example: 09 · Embedded images

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  images: { pixel: 'data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQCAIAAACQkWg2AAAAF0lEQVR4nGPgqMgmCTGMahjVkD1sNQAAjRnrAVbW+rcAAAAASUVORK5CYII=' },
  content: [
    { text: 'One resource, several uses', fontSize: 24, bold: true, margin: [0, 0, 0, 18] },
    'Use the images dictionary to reuse embedded PNG or JPEG data.',
    { image: 'pixel', width: 30, margin: [0, 15, 0, 15] },
    { image: 'pixel', fit: [60, 60] }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  images: { pixel: 'data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABAAAAAQCAIAAACQkWg2AAAAF0lEQVR4nGPgqMgmCTGMahjVkD1sNQAAjRnrAVbW+rcAAAAASUVORK5CYII=' },
  content: [
    { text: 'One resource, several uses', fontSize: 24, bold: true, margin: [0, 0, 0, 18] },
    'Use the images dictionary to reuse embedded PNG or JPEG data.',
    { image: 'pixel', width: 30, margin: [0, 15, 0, 15] },
    { image: 'pixel', fit: [60, 60] }
  ]
};
```

[See the rendered PDF and edit this example](https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/playground/?example=images)



## Choose sizing behavior

| Fields on the image node | Result |
| --- | --- |
| No width, height or fit | Use the image's natural dimensions |
| `width: 150` | Scale proportionally to that width |
| `height: 100` | Scale proportionally to that height; since 0.3.2 |
| `width: 150, height: 100` | Force those dimensions, which can stretch the image |
| `fit: [150, 100]` | Fit inside a rectangle while preserving aspect ratio |
| `cover: { width: 150, height: 100, align: 'right', valign: 'bottom' }` | Fill a rectangle with cropping and alignment |

Display dimensions do not reduce the original image payload. Resize oversized
source images before embedding them when output size and memory matter.

## Select a source for your runtime

| Source | Setup |
| --- | --- |
| Data URL | Put a complete PNG/JPEG base64 data URL in `images` or directly on a node |
| Local file | Node.js only, or a file already present in a browser VFS |
| HTTP(S) URL | Use a named `images` entry and allow it through the resource policy |
| URL with headers | Use `{ url, headers }` in the named `images` entry |

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  images: {
    logo: '/application-owned/assets/logo.png',
    remote: {
      url: 'https://assets.example.com/photo.jpg',
      headers: { 'X-Example-Header': 'value' }
    }
  },
  content: [
    { image: 'logo', width: 120 },
    { image: 'remote', fit: [200, 150] }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  images: {
    logo: '/application-owned/assets/logo.png',
    remote: {
      url: 'https://assets.example.com/photo.jpg',
      headers: { 'X-Example-Header': 'value' }
    }
  },
  content: [
    { image: 'logo', width: 120 },
    { image: 'remote', fit: [200, 150] }
  ]
};
```

This snippet describes source shapes, not a self-contained runnable download.
Supply an existing application-owned file and a real approved URL. In a browser,
the local filename must exist in the VFS; browser URLs also require CORS support.
Do not place private credentials in client-side definitions. The embedded example
above is self-contained and needs no network resource.

## Diagnose missing images

An empty or invalid image value is an error. Check the dictionary key, full data
URL prefix and bytes, file existence, URL response and access policy. Configuring
`setUrlAccessPolicy` does not bypass CORS. A local file policy must allow the actual
resolved file path. See [resource security](/docs/0.3/guides/resource-security/)
and [troubleshooting](/docs/0.3/guides/troubleshooting/).

---

# Links

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/links/

To add external or internal links, use the following syntax:
**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = { content: [
{ text: 'google', link: 'http://google.com' },
{ text: 'Go to page 2', linkToPage: 2 },
{ text: 'Go to Header', linkToDestination: 'header' },
{ text: 'Header content', id: 'header' },
] };
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = { content: [
{ text: 'google', link: 'http://google.com' },
{ text: 'Go to page 2', linkToPage: 2 },
{ text: 'Go to Header', linkToDestination: 'header' },
{ text: 'Header content', id: 'header' },
] };
```
Or link to local computer file:
**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
	content: [
		{
		    text: 'link',
		    link: 'file:///c:/testFile.txt'
		}
	]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
	content: [
		{
		    text: 'link',
		    link: 'file:///c:/testFile.txt'
		}
	]
};
```

## Properties

- `link` (`string`) - URL to external site
- `linkToPage` (`number`) - link to page number
- `linkToDestination` (`string`) - link to document destination

---

# Lists

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/lists/

pdfmake supports both numbered and bulleted lists:

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    'Bulleted list example:',
    {
      // to treat a paragraph as a bulleted list, set an array of items under the ul key
      ul: [
        'Item 1',
        'Item 2',
        'Item 3',
        { text: 'Item 4', bold: true },
      ]
    },

    'Numbered list example:',
    {
      // for numbered lists set the ol key
      ol: [
        'Item 1',
        'Item 2',
        'Item 3'
      ]
    },

    'Colored unordered list:',
    {
      color: 'blue',
      ul: [
          'item 1',
          'item 2',
          'item 3'
      ]
    },

    'Colored unordered list with own marker color:',
    {
      color: 'blue',
      markerColor: 'red',
      ul: [
          'item 1',
          'item 2',
          { text: 'item 3 with custom marker color', markerColor: 'lime' } // Minimal pdfmake version: 0.3.2
      ]
    },

    'Colored ordered list',
    {
      color: 'blue',
      ol: [
          'item 1',
          'item 2',
          'item 3'
      ]
    },
    'Colored ordered list with own marker color:',
    {
      color: 'blue',
      markerColor: 'red',
      ol: [
          'item 1',
          'item 2',
          { text: 'item 3 with custom marker color', markerColor: 'lime' } // Minimal pdfmake version: 0.3.2
      ]
    },
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    'Bulleted list example:',
    {
      // to treat a paragraph as a bulleted list, set an array of items under the ul key
      ul: [
        'Item 1',
        'Item 2',
        'Item 3',
        { text: 'Item 4', bold: true },
      ]
    },

    'Numbered list example:',
    {
      // for numbered lists set the ol key
      ol: [
        'Item 1',
        'Item 2',
        'Item 3'
      ]
    },

    'Colored unordered list:',
    {
      color: 'blue',
      ul: [
          'item 1',
          'item 2',
          'item 3'
      ]
    },

    'Colored unordered list with own marker color:',
    {
      color: 'blue',
      markerColor: 'red',
      ul: [
          'item 1',
          'item 2',
          { text: 'item 3 with custom marker color', markerColor: 'lime' } // Minimal pdfmake version: 0.3.2
      ]
    },

    'Colored ordered list',
    {
      color: 'blue',
      ol: [
          'item 1',
          'item 2',
          'item 3'
      ]
    },
    'Colored ordered list with own marker color:',
    {
      color: 'blue',
      markerColor: 'red',
      ol: [
          'item 1',
          'item 2',
          { text: 'item 3 with custom marker color', markerColor: 'lime' } // Minimal pdfmake version: 0.3.2
      ]
    },
  ]
};
```

# Margins

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/margins/

Any element in pdfMake can have a margin:

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = { content: [
// margin: [left, top, right, bottom]
{ text: 'sample', margin: [ 5, 2, 10, 20 ] },

// margin: [horizontal, vertical]
{ text: 'another text', margin: [5, 2] },

// margin: equalLeftTopRightBottom
{ text: 'last one', margin: 5 },

// single-side margins
{ text: 'sample', marginLeft: 5, marginTop: 2, marginRight: 10, marginBottom: 2 },
] };
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = { content: [
// margin: [left, top, right, bottom]
{ text: 'sample', margin: [ 5, 2, 10, 20 ] },

// margin: [horizontal, vertical]
{ text: 'another text', margin: [5, 2] },

// margin: equalLeftTopRightBottom
{ text: 'last one', margin: 5 },

// single-side margins
{ text: 'sample', marginLeft: 5, marginTop: 2, marginRight: 10, marginBottom: 2 },
] };
```

# Outlines / Bookmarks

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/outlines/

> **Note:** Minimal version: **0.3.5**


PDF Outlines (also called Bookmarks) are a hierarchical navigation structure embedded in a PDF document that allows users to quickly jump to specific pages. They function as an interactive table of contents, typically displayed in the PDF viewer’s navigation panel.

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    {
      text: 'First header in bookmarks',
      outline: true,
    },
    {
      text: 'Second header with custom bookmark',
      outline: true,
      outlineText: 'Custom bookmark text',
    },
    {
      text: 'Structured bookmarks',
      id: 'structured-bookmarks',
      outline: true,
      outlineExpanded: true
    },
    {
      text: 'First subheader',
      outline: true,
      outlineParentId: 'structured-bookmarks'
    },
    {
      text: 'Second subheader',
      outline: true,
      outlineParentId: 'structured-bookmarks'
    },
    {
      text: 'Third subheader',
      outline: true,
      outlineParentId: 'structured-bookmarks',
      id: 'third-subheader'
    }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    {
      text: 'First header in bookmarks',
      outline: true,
    },
    {
      text: 'Second header with custom bookmark',
      outline: true,
      outlineText: 'Custom bookmark text',
    },
    {
      text: 'Structured bookmarks',
      id: 'structured-bookmarks',
      outline: true,
      outlineExpanded: true
    },
    {
      text: 'First subheader',
      outline: true,
      outlineParentId: 'structured-bookmarks'
    },
    {
      text: 'Second subheader',
      outline: true,
      outlineParentId: 'structured-bookmarks'
    },
    {
      text: 'Third subheader',
      outline: true,
      outlineParentId: 'structured-bookmarks',
      id: 'third-subheader'
    }
  ]
};
```

## Properties

- `outline: boolean` - set to `true` for add to bookmarks
- `outlineText: string` (optional) - set custom bookmark text, otherwise text from node
- `outlineExpanded: boolean` (optional) - set to `true` for expanded/opened bookmark
- `outlineParentId: string` (optional) - parent bookmark `id`

---

# Page dimensions, orientation and margins

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/page/

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  // a string or { width: number, height: number }
  pageSize: 'A5',

  // by default we use portrait, you can change it to landscape if you wish
  pageOrientation: 'landscape',

  // [left, top, right, bottom] or [horizontal, vertical] or just a number for equal margins
  pageMargins: [ 40, 60, 40, 60 ],
  content: ['Page size, orientation and margins.']
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  // a string or { width: number, height: number }
  pageSize: 'A5',

  // by default we use portrait, you can change it to landscape if you wish
  pageOrientation: 'landscape',

  // [left, top, right, bottom] or [horizontal, vertical] or just a number for equal margins
  pageMargins: [ 40, 60, 40, 60 ],
  content: ['Page size, orientation and margins.']
};
```

If you set `pageSize` to a string, you can use one of the following values:

* `'4A0'`, `'2A0'`, `'A0'`, `'A1'`, `'A2'`, `'A3'`, `'A4'`, `'A5'`, `'A6'`, `'A7'`, `'A8'`, `'A9'`, `'A10'`,
* `'B0'`, `'B1'`, `'B2'`, `'B3'`, `'B4'`, `'B5'`, `'B6'`, `'B7'`, `'B8'`, `'B9'`, `'B10'`,
* `'C0'`, `'C1'`, `'C2'`, `'C3'`, `'C4'`, `'C5'`, `'C6'`, `'C7'`, `'C8'`, `'C9'`, `'C10'`,
* `'RA0'`, `'RA1'`, `'RA2'`, `'RA3'`, `'RA4'`,
* `'SRA0'`, `'SRA1'`, `'SRA2'`, `'SRA3'`, `'SRA4'`,
* `'EXECUTIVE'`, `'FOLIO'`, `'LEGAL'`, `'LETTER'`, `'TABLOID'`

To change page orientation within a document, add a page break with the new page orientation.

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  pageOrientation: 'portrait',
  content: [
    {text: 'Text on Portrait'},
    {text: 'Text on Landscape', pageOrientation: 'landscape', pageBreak: 'before'},
    {text: 'Text on Landscape 2', pageOrientation: 'portrait', pageBreak: 'after'},
    {text: 'Text on Portrait 2'},
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  pageOrientation: 'portrait',
  content: [
    {text: 'Text on Portrait'},
    {text: 'Text on Landscape', pageOrientation: 'landscape', pageBreak: 'before'},
    {text: 'Text on Landscape 2', pageOrientation: 'portrait', pageBreak: 'after'},
    {text: 'Text on Portrait 2'},
  ]
};
```

Automatic page height:

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  pageSize: {
    width: 595.28,
    height: 'auto'
  },
  content: [
    // ...
  ]
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  pageSize: {
    width: 595.28,
    height: 'auto'
  },
  content: [
    // ...
  ]
}
```


## Dynamically control page breaks, for instance to avoid orphan children

A `pageBreakBefore` function can be specified, which can determine if a page break should be inserted before a node. To implement a 'no orphan child' rule, use a definition like this:

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
    content: [
       {text: '1 Headline', headlineLevel: 1},
       'Some long text of variable length ...',
       {text: '2 Headline', headlineLevel: 1},
       'Some long text of variable length ...',
       {text: '3 Headline', headlineLevel: 1},
       'Some long text of variable length ...',
    ],
  pageBreakBefore: function(currentNode, nodeContainer) {
    // nodeContainer.getFollowingNodesOnPage();
    // nodeContainer.getNodesOnNextPage();
    // nodeContainer.getPreviousNodesOnPage();

    return currentNode.headlineLevel === 1 && nodeContainer.getFollowingNodesOnPage().length === 0;
  }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    content: [
       {text: '1 Headline', headlineLevel: 1},
       'Some long text of variable length ...',
       {text: '2 Headline', headlineLevel: 1},
       'Some long text of variable length ...',
       {text: '3 Headline', headlineLevel: 1},
       'Some long text of variable length ...',
    ],
  pageBreakBefore: function(currentNode, nodeContainer) {
    // nodeContainer.getFollowingNodesOnPage();
    // nodeContainer.getNodesOnNextPage();
    // nodeContainer.getPreviousNodesOnPage();

    return currentNode.headlineLevel === 1 && nodeContainer.getFollowingNodesOnPage().length === 0;
  }
}
```

If `pageBreakBefore` returns true, a page break will be added before the `currentNode`. Current node has the following information attached:

**JavaScript**

```js
const currentNode = {
   id: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   headlineLevel: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   text: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   ul: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   ol: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   table: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   image: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   qr: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   canvas: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   columns: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   style: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   pageOrientation: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   pageNumbers: [2, 3], // The pages this element is visible on (e.g. multi-line text could be on more than one page)
   pages: 6, // the total number of pages of this document
   stack: false, // if this is an element which encapsulates multiple sub-objects
   startPosition: {
     pageNumber: 2, // the page this node starts on
     pageOrientation: 'landscape', // the orientation of this page
     left: 60, // the left position
     right: 60, // the right position
     verticalRatio: 0.2, // the ratio of space used vertically in this document (excluding margins)
     horizontalRatio: 0.0  // the ratio of space used horizontally in this document (excluding margins)
   }
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const currentNode = {
   id: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   headlineLevel: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   text: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   ul: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   ol: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   table: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   image: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   qr: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   canvas: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   columns: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   style: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   pageOrientation: '<as specified in doc definition>',
   pageNumbers: [2, 3], // The pages this element is visible on (e.g. multi-line text could be on more than one page)
   pages: 6, // the total number of pages of this document
   stack: false, // if this is an element which encapsulates multiple sub-objects
   startPosition: {
     pageNumber: 2, // the page this node starts on
     pageOrientation: 'landscape', // the orientation of this page
     left: 60, // the left position
     right: 60, // the right position
     verticalRatio: 0.2, // the ratio of space used vertically in this document (excluding margins)
     horizontalRatio: 0.0  // the ratio of space used horizontally in this document (excluding margins)
   }
};
```

# Patterns

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/patterns/

Patterns can be defined as a dictionary of predefined patterns in the document definition.

Only tiling patterns are supported.

## Pattern definition

Each pattern is defined using:

- `boundingBox` - bounding box used to clip the pattern cell
- `xStep` - horizontal spacing between cells
- `yStep` - vertical spacing between cells
- `pattern` - a PDF stream of operations that render the graphics/text of the cell

For more information on each property and patterns in general see the [PDF reference](https://www.adobe.com/content/dam/acom/en/devnet/pdf/pdfs/pdf_reference_archives/PDFReference.pdf), section 4.6 and 4.6.2 specifically on tiling patterns.

## Pattern definition example

Basic pattern that produces a 45° stripe pattern:

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: ["..."],
  patterns: {
    stripe45d: {
      boundingBox: [1, 1, 4, 4],
      xStep: 3,
      yStep: 3,
      pattern: "1 w 0 1 m 4 5 l s 2 0 m 5 3 l s",
    },
  },
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: ["..."],
  patterns: {
    stripe45d: {
      boundingBox: [1, 1, 4, 4],
      xStep: 3,
      yStep: 3,
      pattern: "1 w 0 1 m 4 5 l s 2 0 m 5 3 l s",
    },
  },
};
```

The output can be seen in the vector example.

## Usage in vectors, tables and text

The following properties are available.

For text:

- `background` - set as background for text (see styling_properties example)

For vectors:

- `color` - set as fill for a vector (see the rectangle in vector example)

For table cells:

- `fillColor` - cell (background) fill color
- `overlayPattern` - overlay for a cell, painted over the contents
- `overlayOpacity` - the opacity of the overlay

Each of the above properties is defined as a tuple `[string, string]`. The first element is the key in the patterns dictionary and the second is the color to use to paint the pattern.

## Examples

Text:

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = { content: [
{ text: 'Insert lorem. And ipsum', background: ['stripe45d', 'gray'] }
] };
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = { content: [
{ text: 'Insert lorem. And ipsum', background: ['stripe45d', 'gray'] }
] };
```

Vector:

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = { content: [{ canvas: [
{
  type: 'rect',
  x: 10, y: 250, w: 50, h: 30,
  color: ['stripe45d', 'blue'],
}
] }] };
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = { content: [{ canvas: [
{
  type: 'rect',
  x: 10, y: 250, w: 50, h: 30,
  color: ['stripe45d', 'blue'],
}
] }] };
```

Table (as used in table cells):

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = { content: [
{
  text: 'Sample value',
  fillOpacity: 0.85,
  fillColor: ['stripe45d', 'blue']
}
] };
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = { content: [
{
  text: 'Sample value',
  fillOpacity: 0.85,
  fillColor: ['stripe45d', 'blue']
}
] };
```

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = { content: [
{
  text: 'Sample value',
  fillOpacity: 0.15,
  fillColor: 'blue',
  overlayPattern: ['stripe45d', 'gray'],
  overlayOpacity: 0.15
}
] };
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { ContentText } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

// Cell properties are included in the bundled pdfmake declarations.
const cell = {
  text: 'Sample value',
  fillOpacity: 0.15,
  fillColor: 'blue',
  overlayPattern: ['stripe45d', 'gray'],
  overlayOpacity: 0.15
} satisfies ContentText;

```

# PDF/A

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/pdfa/

PDF/A is specialized for use in the archiving and long-term preservation of electronic documents.

PDF version 1.4 or above is required.

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
    version: '1.5',
    subset: 'PDF/A-3a',
    tagged: true,
    displayTitle: true,
    info: {
        title: 'Awesome PDF document from pdfmake'
    },
    content: [
        'PDF/A document for archive'
    ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    version: '1.5',
    subset: 'PDF/A-3a',
    tagged: true,
    displayTitle: true,
    info: {
        title: 'Awesome PDF document from pdfmake'
    },
    content: [
        'PDF/A document for archive'
    ]
};
```

Supported PDF versions (property `version`):
- `1.3` - PDF version 1.3 (default) **not supported PDF/A**
- `1.4` - PDF version 1.4
- `1.5` - PDF version 1.5
- `1.6` - PDF version 1.6
- `1.7` - PDF version 1.7
- `1.7ext3` - PDF version 1.7 ExtensionLevel 3

Subset of document (property `subset`):
- `PDF/A-1` (shortcut for PDF/A-1b)
- `PDF/A-1a`
- `PDF/A-1b`
- `PDF/A-2` (shortcut for PDF/A-2b)
- `PDF/A-2a`
- `PDF/A-2b`
- `PDF/A-3` (shortcut for PDF/A-3b)
- `PDF/A-3a`
- `PDF/A-3b`
- `PDF/UA`

Mark document as Tagged PDF (property `tagged`)
- `true` - enable
- `false` - disable

Display of document title in window title (property `displayTitle`)
- `true` - enable
- `false` - disable

---

# QR code

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/qr/

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    // basic usage
    { qr: 'text in QR' },

    // colored QR
    { qr: 'text in QR', foreground: 'red', background: 'yellow' },

    // resized QR
    { qr: 'text in QR', fit: 500 },
  ]
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    // basic usage
    { qr: 'text in QR' },

    // colored QR
    { qr: 'text in QR', foreground: 'red', background: 'yellow' },

    // resized QR
    { qr: 'text in QR', fit: 500 },
  ]
}
```

Properties:

* `qr`: `string` - text in QR code
* `foreground`: `string` (optional, default black) - foreground color
* `background`: `string` (optional, default white) - background color
* `fit`: `integer` (optional) - fit the output QR image
* `version`: `integer` (optional) - QR version range from 1 to 40 (for details see [wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code#Storage)
* `eccLevel`: `string` (optional, default L) - error correction capability (for details see [wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code#Error_correction)), possible values:
  * _L_ - Level L (Low), approx 7% of codewords can be restored
  * _M_ - Level M (Medium), approx 15% of codewords can be restored
  * _Q_ - Level Q (Quartile), approx 25% of codewords can be restored
  * _H_ - Level H (High), approx 30% of codewords can be restored
* `mode`: `string` (optional) - encoding mode, possible values: _numeric_, _alphanumeric, octet_ (for details see [wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code#Storage))
* `mask`: `integer` (optional) - mask pattern, range from 0 to 7 (for details see [wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code#Encoding))

---

# Document sections

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/sections/

Document sections allow you to divide a document into multiple parts, each with its own page settings.

Each section support:
- custom page size and orientation
- custom page margin
- custom header/footer
- custom watermark
- custom background

Definition including all properties:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
    content: [
        {
            header: function (currentPage, pageCount) {
                return currentPage.toString() + ' of ' + pageCount;
            },
            footer: function (currentPage, pageCount) {
                return currentPage.toString() + ' of ' + pageCount;
            },
            background: function () {
                return {text: 'background', alignment: 'right'};
            },
            watermark: 'watermark',
            pageSize: 'A4',
            pageOrientation: 'landscape',
            pageMargins: 5,
            section: [
                'Text in section.'
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    content: [
        {
            header: function (currentPage, pageCount) {
                return currentPage.toString() + ' of ' + pageCount;
            },
            footer: function (currentPage, pageCount) {
                return currentPage.toString() + ' of ' + pageCount;
            },
            background: function () {
                return {text: 'background', alignment: 'right'};
            },
            watermark: 'watermark',
            pageSize: 'A4',
            pageOrientation: 'landscape',
            pageMargins: 5,
            section: [
                'Text in section.'
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

In the next section, properties can be inherited from the previous section:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
    content: [
        {
            header: 'inherit',
            footer: 'inherit',
            background: 'inherit',
            watermark: 'inherit',
            pageSize: 'inherit',
            pageOrientation: 'inherit',
            pageMargins: 'inherit',
            section: [
                'Text in section.'
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    content: [
        {
            header: 'inherit',
            footer: 'inherit',
            background: 'inherit',
            watermark: 'inherit',
            pageSize: 'inherit',
            pageOrientation: 'inherit',
            pageMargins: 'inherit',
            section: [
                'Text in section.'
            ]
        }
    ]
}
```

Full example is available in [examples/section.js](https://github.com/bpampuch/pdfmake/blob/master/examples/sections.js).

---

# Encryption and access privileges

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/security/

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  userPassword: '123',
  ownerPassword: '123456',
  permissions: {
    printing: 'highResolution', //'lowResolution'
    modifying: false,
    copying: false,
    annotating: true,
    fillingForms: true,
    contentAccessibility: true,
    documentAssembly: true
  },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  userPassword: '123',
  ownerPassword: '123456',
  permissions: {
    printing: 'highResolution', //'lowResolution'
    modifying: false,
    copying: false,
    annotating: true,
    fillingForms: true,
    contentAccessibility: true,
    documentAssembly: true
  },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

PDF document allow you to encrypt the PDF file and require a password when opening the file,
and/or set permissions of what users can do with the PDF file.

To enable encryption set user password in `userPassword` (string value). The PDF file will
be encrypted when a user password is provided, and users will be prompted to enter the password
to decrypt the file when opening it.

To set access privileges for the PDF file, you need to provide an owner password in `ownerPassword` (string value)
and object `permissions` with permissions. By default, all operations are disallowed.
You need to explicitly allow certain operations.

Following settings are allowed in `permissions` object:

- `printing` - whether printing is allowed. Specify `"lowResolution"` to allow degraded printing, or `"highResolution"` to allow printing with high resolution
- `modifying` - whether modifying the file is allowed. Specify `true` to allow modifying document content
- `copying` - whether copying text or graphics is allowed. Specify `true` to allow copying
- `annotating` - whether annotating, form filling is allowed. Specify `true` to allow annotating and form filling
- `fillingForms` - whether form filling and signing is allowed. Specify `true` to allow filling in form fields and signing
- `contentAccessibility` - whether copying text for accessibility is allowed. Specify `true` to allow copying for accessibility
- `documentAssembly` - whether assembling document is allowed. Specify `true` to allow document assembly

You can specify either user password, owner password or both passwords.
Behavior differs according to passwords you provides:

- When only user password is provided,
  users with user password are able to decrypt the file and have full access to the document.
- When only owner password is provided,
  users are able to decrypt and open the document without providing any password,
  but the access is limited to those operations explicitly permitted.
  Users with owner password have full access to the document.
- When both passwords are provided,
  users with user password are able to decrypt the file
  but only have limited access to the file according to permission settings.
  Users with owner password have full access to the document.

Note that PDF file itself cannot enforce access privileges.
When file is decrypted, PDF viewer applications have full access to the file content,
and it is up to viewer applications to respect permission settings.

To choose encryption method, you need to specify PDF version by `version`.
The best possible encryption method for PDF version is used.


> **Note:** PDF version is used only for encryption method, all other PDF elements are in version 1.3.


Available versions:

- `1.3` - PDF version 1.3 (default), 40-bit RC4 is used
- `1.4` - PDF version 1.4, 128-bit RC4 is used
- `1.5` - PDF version 1.5, 128-bit RC4 is used
- `1.6` - PDF version 1.6, 128-bit AES is used
- `1.7` - PDF version 1.7, 128-bit AES is used
- `1.7ext3` - PDF version 1.7 ExtensionLevel 3, 256-bit AES is used

When using PDF version 1.7 ExtensionLevel 3, password is truncated to 127 bytes of its UTF-8 representation.
In older versions, password is truncated to 32 bytes, and only Latin-1 characters are allowed.

---

# Snaking columns

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/snaking-columns/

> **Note:** Minimal version: **0.3.5**


Snaking columns (or newspaper-style columns) are a column layout mode where content flows vertically through the first column, then continues at the top of the next column, alternating direction as needed. Instead of always restarting at the top for each new row of columns, the layout "snakes" through the available columns in a continuous reading order.

When `snakingColumns: true` is enabled, only the **first column** should contain content. Subsequent columns serve as empty placeholders for overflow.

**JavaScript**

```js
var myLongContent = 'A paragraph flowing through snaking columns. '.repeat(120);
var docDefinition = {
    content: [
        {
            columns: [
                {text: myLongContent, width: '*'},  // Content goes here
                {text: '', width: '*'},             // Empty overflow target
                {text: '', width: '*'}              // Empty overflow target
            ],
            snakingColumns: true
        }
    ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var myLongContent = 'A paragraph flowing through snaking columns. '.repeat(120);
var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    content: [
        {
            columns: [
                {text: myLongContent, width: '*'},  // Content goes here
                {text: '', width: '*'},             // Empty overflow target
                {text: '', width: '*'}              // Empty overflow target
            ],
            snakingColumns: true
        }
    ]
};
```

Nesting a "snaking column" directly inside another "snaking column" (a recursive snaking layout) is not supported.

**Recommendation**:
- Avoid deep nesting of snaking columns within other snaking columns.
- Standard columns (non-snaking) _can_ be safely nested inside snaking columns.
- Snaking columns _can_ be safely nested inside standard columns.

---

# Stack of paragraphs

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/stack/

You could have figured out by now (from the examples), that if you set the ```content``` key to an array, the  document becomes a stack of paragraphs.

You'll quite often reuse this structure in a nested element, like in the following example:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    'paragraph 1',
    'paragraph 2',
    {
      columns: [
        'first column is a simple text',
        [
          // second column consists of paragraphs
          'paragraph A',
          'paragraph B',
          'these paragraphs will be rendered one below another inside the column'
        ]
      ]
    }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    'paragraph 1',
    'paragraph 2',
    {
      columns: [
        'first column is a simple text',
        [
          // second column consists of paragraphs
          'paragraph A',
          'paragraph B',
          'these paragraphs will be rendered one below another inside the column'
        ]
      ]
    }
  ]
};
```

The problem with an array is that you cannot add styling properties to it (to change fontSize for example).

The good news is - array is just a shortcut in pdfMake for { stack: [] }, so if you want to restyle the whole stack, you can do it using the expanded definition:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    'paragraph 1',
    'paragraph 2',
    {
      columns: [
        'first column is a simple text',
        {
          stack: [
            // second column consists of paragraphs
            'paragraph A',
            'paragraph B',
            'these paragraphs will be rendered one below another inside the column'
          ],
          fontSize: 15
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    'paragraph 1',
    'paragraph 2',
    {
      columns: [
        'first column is a simple text',
        {
          stack: [
            // second column consists of paragraphs
            'paragraph A',
            'paragraph B',
            'these paragraphs will be rendered one below another inside the column'
          ],
          fontSize: 15
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
};
```

---

# Styling

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/styling/

## Style a block or an inline run

A string is a plain paragraph. Use a text node to add properties. Use a `text`
array for differently styled runs within the **same paragraph**; a content array
or stack creates separate blocks.



### Runnable example: 04 · Text & named styles

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  content: [
    { text: 'Style with intent', style: 'heading' },
    { text: ['One paragraph with ', { text: 'bold', bold: true }, ' and ', { text: 'italic', italics: true }, ' inline text.'] },
    { text: 'A reusable note style.', style: 'note' },
    { ul: ['Readable defaults', 'Small style dictionaries', 'Consistent spacing'], margin: [0, 12, 0, 0] }
  ],
  defaultStyle: { fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 1.3 },
  styles: {
    heading: { fontSize: 26, bold: true, color: '#08786b', margin: [0, 0, 0, 18] },
    note: { fontSize: 10, color: '#536771', margin: [0, 12, 0, 0] }
  }
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    { text: 'Style with intent', style: 'heading' },
    { text: ['One paragraph with ', { text: 'bold', bold: true }, ' and ', { text: 'italic', italics: true }, ' inline text.'] },
    { text: 'A reusable note style.', style: 'note' },
    { ul: ['Readable defaults', 'Small style dictionaries', 'Consistent spacing'], margin: [0, 12, 0, 0] }
  ],
  defaultStyle: { fontSize: 12, lineHeight: 1.3 },
  styles: {
    heading: { fontSize: 26, bold: true, color: '#08786b', margin: [0, 0, 0, 18] },
    note: { fontSize: 10, color: '#536771', margin: [0, 12, 0, 0] }
  }
};
```

[See the rendered PDF and edit this example](https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/playground/?example=styles)



## Reuse named styles

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  defaultStyle: { fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 1.2 },
  styles: {
    heading: { fontSize: 24, bold: true },
    muted: { color: '#536771' },
    subheading: { extends: 'heading', fontSize: 16 }
  },
  content: [
    { text: 'A heading', style: 'heading' },
    { text: 'A muted heading', style: ['heading', 'muted'] },
    { text: 'An explicit override', style: 'heading', fontSize: 18 },
    { text: 'A subheading', style: 'subheading' }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  defaultStyle: { fontSize: 11, lineHeight: 1.2 },
  styles: {
    heading: { fontSize: 24, bold: true },
    muted: { color: '#536771' },
    subheading: { extends: 'heading', fontSize: 16 }
  },
  content: [
    { text: 'A heading', style: 'heading' },
    { text: 'A muted heading', style: ['heading', 'muted'] },
    { text: 'An explicit override', style: 'heading', fontSize: 18 },
    { text: 'A subheading', style: 'subheading' }
  ]
};
```

`style` refers to entries in `styles`. Later styles in an array take precedence
when they define the same property. Explicit node properties take precedence over
its named styles. `defaultStyle` supplies document defaults. Styles on containers
can be inherited by their children; explicit child properties override them.

Named-style `extends` is available since **0.3.3**. It accepts one parent name or
an array. A style's own properties win over its parents; later parent entries
take precedence when several parents supply the same property. Keep inheritance
short and acyclic so the result is easy to understand.

## Common text properties

| Property | Type / values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `font` | Registered family name | Must match your font map |
| `fontSize` | Number, points | Text size |
| `bold`, `italics` | Boolean, default false | Select the corresponding font variant |
| `alignment` | `'left'`, `'center'`, `'right'`, `'justify'` | Paragraph alignment |
| `lineHeight` | Number, default 1 | Line-height multiplier |
| `color`, `background` | Color name or hex string | Text color and text background |
| `characterSpacing` | Number, points | Additional spacing between characters |
| `wordBreak` | `'normal'` (default), `'break-all'` | Wrapping behavior |
| `fontFeatures` | String array | Font-specific typographic features |
| `style` | String or string array | Named styles to apply |
| `markerColor` | Color | Bullet marker color |

Named colors and hex values such as `'#08786b'` are supported. Font features
depend on the selected font. Selecting `bold` or `italics` requires the variant
to be registered; setting a flag does not supply a missing font file.

## Decorations

| Property | Type / values |
| --- | --- |
| `decoration` | `'underline'`, `'lineThrough'`, `'overline'`, or an array |
| `decorationStyle` | `'solid'`, `'dashed'`, `'dotted'`, `'double'`, `'wavy'` |
| `decorationColor` | Color |
| `decorationThickness` | Numeric width; since 0.3.3 |

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  content: [{ text: 'A marked passage', decoration: 'underline', decorationStyle: 'wavy', decorationColor: '#08786b' }]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [{ text: 'A marked passage', decoration: 'underline', decorationStyle: 'wavy', decorationColor: '#08786b' }]
};
```

## Styles are not CSS

Use pdfmake's documented field names. There is no CSS cascade, DOM selector or
browser box model. Margins use point values and `[left, top, right, bottom]` order.
To style several blocks together, use a [stack](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/stack/).
See [fonts](/docs/0.3/fonts/) for variant registration and character coverage.

---

# SVGs

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/svgs/

SVGs are much like [images](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/images/) except it is not currently possible to refer to SVGs by file or re-use from a dictionary.


> **Note:** The SVG node expects a valid SVG value. If the value is invalid or empty, an error is thrown.


Library [SVG-to-PDFKit](https://github.com/alafr/SVG-to-PDFKit) is used to transformation from SVG to PDF document.

Node `svg` value can be string or `SVGElement` object (is available only in browser).


> **Note:** Support of `SVGElement` object required version **0.3.1** or later


**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    {
      // If no width/height/fit is used, then dimensions from the svg element is used.
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>'
    },
    {
      // if you specify width, svg will scale proportionally
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>',
      width: 150
    },
    {
      // if you specify height, svg will scale proportionally
      // Minimal pdfmake version: 0.3.2
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>',
      height: 100
    },
    {
      // if you specify both width and height - svg will be stretched
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>',
      width: 600,
      height: 400
    },
    {
      // you can also fit the svg inside a rectangle
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>',
      fit: [150, 100]
    },
    {
      // if no width/height is specified in SVG element, you must set width and height for node
      svg: '<svg>...</svg>',
      width: 300,
      height: 200
    },
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    {
      // If no width/height/fit is used, then dimensions from the svg element is used.
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>'
    },
    {
      // if you specify width, svg will scale proportionally
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>',
      width: 150
    },
    {
      // if you specify height, svg will scale proportionally
      // Minimal pdfmake version: 0.3.2
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>',
      height: 100
    },
    {
      // if you specify both width and height - svg will be stretched
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>',
      width: 600,
      height: 400
    },
    {
      // you can also fit the svg inside a rectangle
      svg: '<svg width="300" height="200" viewBox="0 0 300 200">...</svg>',
      fit: [150, 100]
    },
    {
      // if no width/height is specified in SVG element, you must set width and height for node
      svg: '<svg>...</svg>',
      width: 300,
      height: 200
    },
  ]
};
```

---

# Tables

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/tables/

## Start with rows and a repeating header

Use a table when cells in different rows need to align. `body` is an array of row
arrays. Each row must have the same number of cells; cells can contain text or
other pdfmake nodes. `headerRows: 1` repeats the first row when the table continues
onto another page.



### Runnable example: 03 · Tables & repeating headers

**JavaScript**

```js
var rows = Array.from({ length: 65 }, (_, i) => [
  'Item ' + (i + 1), 'A row that can continue across pages', String(i + 1)
]);
var dd = {
  content: [
    { text: 'A longer table', fontSize: 24, bold: true, margin: [0, 0, 0, 16] },
    { layout: 'lightHorizontalLines', table: {
      headerRows: 1, widths: [70, '*', 40],
      body: [[{ text: 'Item', bold: true }, { text: 'Description', bold: true }, { text: 'Qty', bold: true }], ...rows]
    } }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var rows = Array.from({ length: 65 }, (_, i) => [
  'Item ' + (i + 1), 'A row that can continue across pages', String(i + 1)
]);
var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    { text: 'A longer table', fontSize: 24, bold: true, margin: [0, 0, 0, 16] },
    { layout: 'lightHorizontalLines', table: {
      headerRows: 1, widths: [70, '*', 40],
      body: [[{ text: 'Item', bold: true }, { text: 'Description', bold: true }, { text: 'Qty', bold: true }], ...rows]
    } }
  ]
};
```

[See the rendered PDF and edit this example](https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/playground/?example=tables)



## Choose widths

| Width | Meaning | Useful when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A number, for example `80` | Fixed points | Codes, counts or a predictable label column |
| `'*'` | Share the remaining width | A description should fill the available space |
| `'auto'` | Measure the content | Short labels should use only the width they need |
| A percentage string | Percentage-based width | A proportional layout is required; test mixed widths carefully |

Borders, padding, page margins and other columns consume space too. Start with
fixed and star widths, then use `auto` where content-based sizing is intentional.
Avoid adding large fixed widths that exceed the content area.

## Table and cell fields

| Field | Where | Type / purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | `table` | Nonempty row arrays |
| `widths` | `table` | Width descriptors, one per column |
| `headerRows` | `table` | Number of leading rows repeated as headers |
| `dontBreakRows` | `table` | Keep an individual row from splitting across pages |
| `keepWithHeaderRows` | `table` | Number of following rows to keep with the header |
| `layout` | Node, beside `table` | Built-in layout name, registered custom name, or layout object |
| `colSpan`, `rowSpan` | Cell | Positive number of columns/rows covered; placeholders are still required |
| `verticalAlignment` | Cell | `'top'` (default), `'middle'` or `'bottom'` |
| `border` | Cell | Four booleans: left, top, right, bottom |
| `borderColor` | Cell | Four colors in the same order |
| `fillColor` | Cell | Background color or a supported pattern tuple |
| `fillOpacity` | Cell | Numeric background opacity |
| `overlayPattern`, `overlayOpacity` | Cell | Pattern tuple and numeric opacity painted over the contents |

Keeping a row together cannot make an oversized row fit on a page. Test long
descriptions and nested content with your actual page size and fonts.

## Merge cells without changing the row length

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  content: [{
    table: {
      widths: ['*', '*', '*'],
      body: [
        [{ text: 'A heading across three columns', colSpan: 3, bold: true }, {}, {}],
        [{ text: 'Two rows', rowSpan: 2 }, 'A', 'B'],
        [{}, 'C', 'D']
      ]
    }
  }]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [{
    table: {
      widths: ['*', '*', '*'],
      body: [
        [{ text: 'A heading across three columns', colSpan: 3, bold: true }, {}, {}],
        [{ text: 'Two rows', rowSpan: 2 }, 'A', 'B'],
        [{}, 'C', 'D']
      ]
    }
  }]
};
```

The empty objects occupy the cells covered by a span. Leaving them out produces
an inconsistent row. Do not use `undefined` as a placeholder. The
[spans playground example](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=spans) shows this definition.

## Use a built-in layout

`noBorders`, `headerLineOnly` and `lightHorizontalLines` are available by name.
Put `layout` beside `table`, not inside it:

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  content: [{
    layout: 'lightHorizontalLines',
    table: { headerRows: 1, widths: ['*', 'auto'], body: [['Item', 'Qty'], ['Notebook', 3]] }
  }]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [{
    layout: 'lightHorizontalLines',
    table: { headerRows: 1, widths: ['*', 'auto'], body: [['Item', 'Qty'], ['Notebook', 3]] }
  }]
};
```

## Register a custom layout

Register layouts before creating the document. In Node use your configured
`pdfmake` singleton; in the browser use `pdfMake`.

**JavaScript**

```js
pdfMake.addTableLayouts({
  compact: {
    hLineWidth: function (index, node) {
      return index === node.table.headerRows ? 1 : 0;
    },
    vLineWidth: function () { return 0; },
    hLineColor: function () { return '#b7cfc4'; },
    paddingLeft: function () { return 6; },
    paddingRight: function () { return 6; }
  }
});

var dd = {
  content: [{ layout: 'compact', table: { headerRows: 1, body: [['Item', 'Qty'], ['Notebook', 3]] } }]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import pdfMake from "pdfmake/build/pdfmake.js";
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

pdfMake.addTableLayouts({
  compact: {
    hLineWidth: function (index, node) {
      return index === node.table.headerRows ? 1 : 0;
    },
    vLineWidth: function () { return 0; },
    hLineColor: function () { return '#b7cfc4'; },
    paddingLeft: function () { return 6; },
    paddingRight: function () { return 6; }
  }
});

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [{ layout: 'compact', table: { headerRows: 1, body: [['Item', 'Qty'], ['Notebook', 3]] } }]
};
```

The snippet assumes the browser engine and fonts are loaded. Defining a layout
variable alone does not register it. Prefer deterministic callbacks; avoid
mutating shared configuration during concurrent Node jobs.

## Diagnose malformed tables

Check `body` before changing borders or widths: it must contain row arrays with
consistent lengths. Check span placeholders next. In the local improvement branch,
diagnostics identify the offending definition path and expected number of cells.
See [errors and diagnostics](/docs/0.3/guides/errors/).

---

# Table of contents

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/toc/

## Mark headings for inclusion

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    { toc: { title: { text: 'Contents', fontSize: 20, bold: true }, numberStyle: { bold: true } } },
    { text: 'Introduction', tocItem: true, fontSize: 18, margin: [0, 20, 0, 10] },
    'Document body',
    { text: 'Details', tocItem: true, pageBreak: 'before', fontSize: 18 }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    { toc: { title: { text: 'Contents', fontSize: 20, bold: true }, numberStyle: { bold: true } } },
    { text: 'Introduction', tocItem: true, fontSize: 18, margin: [0, 20, 0, 10] },
    'Document body',
    { text: 'Details', tocItem: true, pageBreak: 'before', fontSize: 18 }
  ]
};
```

The `toc` node inserts the generated list; `tocItem` marks text nodes for inclusion. Page numbers are calculated during layout.

## Multiple tables of contents

Each ToC is a separate content node. Use IDs to choose which list receives each item:

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: [
    { toc: { id: 'main', title: 'All sections' } },
    { toc: { id: 'details', title: 'Detailed sections' } },
    { text: 'Overview', tocItem: 'main' },
    { text: 'Technical details', tocItem: ['main', 'details'], pageBreak: 'before' }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    { toc: { id: 'main', title: 'All sections' } },
    { toc: { id: 'details', title: 'Detailed sections' } },
    { text: 'Overview', tocItem: 'main' },
    { text: 'Technical details', tocItem: ['main', 'details'], pageBreak: 'before' }
  ]
};
```

Do not put two `toc` keys on the same object; JavaScript retains only the last value.

## ToC options

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Identifier for a named ToC |
| `title` | string or text node | Optional title |
| `textStyle`, `numberStyle` | style object | Entry text and page-number styling |
| `textMargin` | margin | Entry spacing |
| `hideEmpty` | boolean | Hide an empty ToC; default false, since 0.3.3 |
| `sortBy` | `'page'` or `'title'` | Ordering; default page, since 0.3.3 |
| `sortLocale` | string | Locale for sorting; runtime locale by default, since 0.3.3 |
| `outlines` | boolean | Include entries in PDF bookmarks; since 0.3.5 |

On a marked text node, `tocItem` accepts `true`, one ToC ID or an array of IDs. Text-node `textStyle`, `numberStyle` and `textMargin` can customize its entry. See [outlines](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/outlines/) for bookmark controls.

---

# Watermark

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/watermark/

## Properties

* `text` - watermark text
* `color` - color of text
* `opacity` opacity of text
* `bold` - bold style of text
* `italics` - italics style of text
* `fontSize` - own font size of text (ideal size is calculated automatically)
* `angle` - angle of text rotation

## Examples

Example of simple basic usage:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  watermark: 'test watermark',
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  watermark: 'test watermark',
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

Example of font style:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  watermark: { text: 'test watermark', color: 'blue', opacity: 0.3, bold: true, italics: false },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  watermark: { text: 'test watermark', color: 'blue', opacity: 0.3, bold: true, italics: false },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

Example of own font size:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  watermark: { text: 'test watermark', fontSize: 20 },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  watermark: { text: 'test watermark', fontSize: 20 },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

Example of watermark rotation angle:
**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  watermark: { text: 'test watermark', angle: 70 },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  watermark: { text: 'test watermark', angle: 70 },
  content: [
    '...'
  ]
};
```
