# Fonts and character coverage

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/fonts/

## Choose a font strategy

| Runtime | Font source | Setup |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js | Real font files | `addFonts` with absolute paths |
| Node.js | Standard PDF fonts | `require('pdfmake/standard-fonts/Helvetica')` |
| Browser | Bundled Roboto VFS | Load `build/vfs_fonts.js` |
| Browser | Custom VFS or URLs | [Custom browser fonts](/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/) |

The default family is `Roboto`. Node.js does not automatically register its files. Every family should map `normal`, `bold`, `italics` and `bolditalics` to appropriate font data. A style selecting a missing variant can fail even if normal text works.

## Register local fonts in Node.js

This example assumes you have licensed font files in a `fonts` directory beside your CommonJS script:

**JavaScript**

```js
const path = require('node:path');
const pdfmake = require('pdfmake');
const fonts = {
  Roboto: {
    normal: path.join(__dirname, 'fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf'),
    bold: path.join(__dirname, 'fonts/Roboto-Medium.ttf'),
    italics: path.join(__dirname, 'fonts/Roboto-Italic.ttf'),
    bolditalics: path.join(__dirname, 'fonts/Roboto-MediumItalic.ttf')
  }
};
const allowed = new Set(Object.values(fonts.Roboto));
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(file => allowed.has(path.resolve(file)));
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const path = require('node:path');
import pdfmake from "pdfmake";
const fonts = {
  Roboto: {
    normal: path.join(__dirname, 'fonts/Roboto-Regular.ttf'),
    bold: path.join(__dirname, 'fonts/Roboto-Medium.ttf'),
    italics: path.join(__dirname, 'fonts/Roboto-Italic.ttf'),
    bolditalics: path.join(__dirname, 'fonts/Roboto-MediumItalic.ttf')
  }
};
const allowed = new Set(Object.values(fonts.Roboto));
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(file => allowed.has(path.resolve(file)));
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
```

The allowlist is appropriate for application-owned, immutable files. When paths come from untrusted users, also account for symlinks and filesystem permissions. Do not treat a string prefix such as `fonts/` as a secure boundary.

## Match text to glyph coverage

Standard fonts have limited encodings; they do not cover arbitrary Unicode. Choose embedded fonts with the glyphs your actual languages need. A Unicode string alone does not guarantee the selected font can render it. Verify representative characters and all bold/italic variants in generated PDFs.

pdfmake embeds fonts through PDFKit. Include only the browser font families you need; VFS data increases download and parse costs. Respect each font's redistribution and embedding license.

## Related guides

[Standard 14 fonts](/docs/0.3/fonts/standard-14-fonts/) · [Browser VFS](/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/vfs/) · [Font URLs](/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/url/) · [Troubleshooting](/docs/0.3/guides/troubleshooting/)

---

# Custom fonts (client-side)

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/

pdfmake uses the Roboto font by default. This guide explains how to use your own fonts with pdfmake (in client-side code).

## Two ways are now possible:
* [use virtual file system](/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/vfs/)
* [use font file via URL (https:// or http:// protocol)](/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/url/)

---

# via URL protocol

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/url/

To use custom fonts, 2 steps are required:

1. assign `pdfMake.addFonts(...)` your font files accessible via url address in your javascript
2. specify the font in your doc-definition

## 1. assign `pdfMake.addFonts(...)` your font files in your javascript

Font files must be accessible via url address (https:// or http:// protocol). In your code, before calling `pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition)` set `pdfMake.addFonts(...)` as in the example below:

**JavaScript**

```js
var fonts = {
   yourFontName: {
     normal: 'https://example.com/fonts/fontFile.ttf',
     bold: 'https://example.com/fonts/fontFile2.ttf',
     italics: 'https://example.com/fonts/fontFile3.ttf',
     bolditalics: 'https://example.com/fonts/fontFile4.ttf'
   },
   anotherFontName: {

   },

   // download default Roboto font from unpkg.com
   Roboto: {
     normal: 'https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/fonts/Roboto/Roboto-Regular.ttf',
     bold: 'https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/fonts/Roboto/Roboto-Medium.ttf',
     italics: 'https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/fonts/Roboto/Roboto-Italic.ttf',
     bolditalics: 'https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/fonts/Roboto/Roboto-MediumItalic.ttf'
   },

   // example of usage fonts in collection
   PingFangSC: {
     normal: ['https://example.com/fonts/pingfang.ttc', 'PingFangSC-Regular'],
     bold: ['https://example.com/fonts/pingfang.ttc', 'PingFangSC-Semibold'],
   }
};

pdfMake.addFonts(fonts);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
var fonts = {
   yourFontName: {
     normal: 'https://example.com/fonts/fontFile.ttf',
     bold: 'https://example.com/fonts/fontFile2.ttf',
     italics: 'https://example.com/fonts/fontFile3.ttf',
     bolditalics: 'https://example.com/fonts/fontFile4.ttf'
   },
   anotherFontName: {

   },

   // download default Roboto font from unpkg.com
   Roboto: {
     normal: 'https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/fonts/Roboto/Roboto-Regular.ttf',
     bold: 'https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/fonts/Roboto/Roboto-Medium.ttf',
     italics: 'https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/fonts/Roboto/Roboto-Italic.ttf',
     bolditalics: 'https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/fonts/Roboto/Roboto-MediumItalic.ttf'
   },

   // example of usage fonts in collection
   PingFangSC: {
     normal: ['https://example.com/fonts/pingfang.ttc', 'PingFangSC-Regular'],
     bold: ['https://example.com/fonts/pingfang.ttc', 'PingFangSC-Semibold'],
   }
};

pdfMake.addFonts(fonts);
```

## 2. specify the font in your doc-definition

pdfMake uses 'Roboto' as default font, so in order to use your font, you should specify it in your doc-definition object.

The easiest way is to set it globally in the **defaultStyle**

**JavaScript**

```js
var docDefinition = {
  content: ['Example document content'],
  defaultStyle: {
    font: 'yourFontName'
  }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: ['Example document content'],
  defaultStyle: {
    font: 'yourFontName'
  }
}
```

---

# Custom fonts with VFS

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/vfs/

## Build the font container

Use licensed font files that cover your target languages. Place them in your application's `fonts/` directory and generate a VFS file from your project root:

```sh
node node_modules/pdfmake/build-vfs.js ./fonts ./vfs_fonts.js
```

This embeds **all files** in the supplied directory as base64 entries. Keep generated application assets outside `node_modules` so an install cannot overwrite your custom fonts. Rebuild the VFS whenever the font files change. Browser VFS is unnecessary for normal [Node font paths](/docs/0.3/fonts/).

## Load and register

Load the engine before your generated VFS script. The generated script registers its files when `pdfMake` is already available. In a bundler, import the VFS object and call `addVirtualFileSystem` explicitly:

**JavaScript**

```js
import pdfMake from 'pdfmake/build/pdfmake';
import customVfs from './vfs_fonts';

pdfMake.addVirtualFileSystem(customVfs);
pdfMake.addFonts({
  MyFont: {
    normal: 'MyFont-Regular.ttf',
    bold: 'MyFont-Bold.ttf',
    italics: 'MyFont-Italic.ttf',
    bolditalics: 'MyFont-BoldItalic.ttf'
  }
});

await pdfMake.createPdf({
  defaultStyle: { font: 'MyFont' },
  content: ['A document using my font.']
}).download('document.pdf');
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import pdfMake from 'pdfmake/build/pdfmake';
import customVfs from './vfs_fonts';

pdfMake.addVirtualFileSystem(customVfs);
pdfMake.addFonts({
  MyFont: {
    normal: 'MyFont-Regular.ttf',
    bold: 'MyFont-Bold.ttf',
    italics: 'MyFont-Italic.ttf',
    bolditalics: 'MyFont-BoldItalic.ttf'
  }
});

await pdfMake.createPdf({
  defaultStyle: { font: 'MyFont' },
  content: ['A document using my font.']
}).download('document.pdf');
```

Replace these names with the exact keys in your generated VFS. Font family names such as `MyFont` are the names you use in styles; file keys identify embedded files. Define every variant you use. You can map multiple variants to one file when that is intentional, but this does not create a real bold or italic face.

## Font collections

For a supported TrueType collection, a descriptor can be `[filename, faceName]`:

**JavaScript**

```js
pdfMake.addFonts({
  PingFangSC: {
    normal: ['pingfang.ttc', 'PingFangSC-Regular'],
    bold: ['pingfang.ttc', 'PingFangSC-Semibold']
  }
});
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
pdfMake.addFonts({
  PingFangSC: {
    normal: ['pingfang.ttc', 'PingFangSC-Regular'],
    bold: ['pingfang.ttc', 'PingFangSC-Semibold']
  }
});
```

Embed the collection and use valid face names. This example registers normal and bold only; add italic variants before using them.

## Common failures

If a file cannot be found, compare the descriptor filename to the generated VFS keys. If a font is undefined, compare `defaultStyle.font` to the family map. If characters are missing, test the font's glyph coverage. If the browser bundle is large, remove unused families and files from the VFS input directory.

---

# Icons

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/fonts/icons/

- make a font at http://fontello.com/ or something and download it

- from font file (for example .ttf) create vfs_fonts.js file (see how to [use custom fonts](/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/vfs/))

- define font in js (just defining normal might be enough):
**JavaScript**

```js
pdfMake.fonts = {
    Fontello: {
        normal: 'fontello.ttf',
        bold: 'fontello.ttf',
        italics: 'fontello.ttf',
        bolditalics: 'fontello.ttf'
    }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
pdfMake.fonts = {
    Fontello: {
        normal: 'fontello.ttf',
        bold: 'fontello.ttf',
        italics: 'fontello.ttf',
        bolditalics: 'fontello.ttf'
    }
}
```

- add a style for icons:
`            icon: {
                font: 'Fontello'
            }`
- make a text paragraph:
`
            { text: '', style: 'icon' }, //icon wifi`
- as the text you copy from the fontello-codes.css from the comments (not the escaped value)

---

If you need an icon within text, you need to nest text objects:

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = { content: [{
text: [
        { text: '', style: 'icon' }, //icon gift
        " my present"
    ]
}] };
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = { content: [{
text: [
        { text: '', style: 'icon' }, //icon gift
        " my present"
    ]
}] };
```
this puts out: "[gift icon] my present"

---

# Standard 14 fonts

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/fonts/standard-14-fonts/

PDF contains [standard 14 fonts](http://www.enfocus.com/manuals/ReferenceGuide/PS/18/enUS/en-us/common/pse/concept/c_aa1044513.html).

**Character coverage:** Standard fonts use limited encodings and do not support arbitrary Unicode. Use embedded fonts for multilingual documents and test the glyphs you need.

## Use in pdfmake on the server side

**Example of usage:**
**JavaScript**

```js
var fonts = {
  Courier: {
    normal: 'Courier',
    bold: 'Courier-Bold',
    italics: 'Courier-Oblique',
    bolditalics: 'Courier-BoldOblique'
  },
  Helvetica: {
    normal: 'Helvetica',
    bold: 'Helvetica-Bold',
    italics: 'Helvetica-Oblique',
    bolditalics: 'Helvetica-BoldOblique'
  },
  Times: {
    normal: 'Times-Roman',
    bold: 'Times-Bold',
    italics: 'Times-Italic',
    bolditalics: 'Times-BoldItalic'
  },
  Symbol: {
    normal: 'Symbol'
  },
  ZapfDingbats: {
    normal: 'ZapfDingbats'
  }
};

var pdfmake = require('pdfmake');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);

var docDefinition = {
  content: ['First paragraph', 'Another paragraph'],
  defaultStyle: {
    font: 'Helvetica'
  }
};

var pdf = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition);
pdf.write('test.pdf').then(() => {
  // success event
}, err => {
  console.error(err);
});
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var fonts = {
  Courier: {
    normal: 'Courier',
    bold: 'Courier-Bold',
    italics: 'Courier-Oblique',
    bolditalics: 'Courier-BoldOblique'
  },
  Helvetica: {
    normal: 'Helvetica',
    bold: 'Helvetica-Bold',
    italics: 'Helvetica-Oblique',
    bolditalics: 'Helvetica-BoldOblique'
  },
  Times: {
    normal: 'Times-Roman',
    bold: 'Times-Bold',
    italics: 'Times-Italic',
    bolditalics: 'Times-BoldItalic'
  },
  Symbol: {
    normal: 'Symbol'
  },
  ZapfDingbats: {
    normal: 'ZapfDingbats'
  }
};

var pdfmake = require('pdfmake');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);

var docDefinition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: ['First paragraph', 'Another paragraph'],
  defaultStyle: {
    font: 'Helvetica'
  }
};

var pdf = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition);
pdf.write('test.pdf').then(() => {
  // success event
}, err => {
  console.error(err);
});
```


## Use in pdfmake on the client side

Standard font bundles are available in the pdfmake package's `build/standard-fonts/` directory. Include the bundle for each font family you need **after** `pdfmake.min.js`. Each bundle automatically registers its fonts with `pdfMake`.

For example, to use Helvetica:

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/pdfmake.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/pdfmake@0.3.12/build/standard-fonts/Helvetica.js"></script>
<script>
  var docDefinition = {
    content: ['First paragraph', 'Another paragraph'],
    defaultStyle: {
      font: 'Helvetica'
    }
  };

  pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition).download('document.pdf');
</script>
```

The available bundles are `Courier.js`, `Helvetica.js`, `Times.js`, `Symbol.js` and `ZapfDingbats.js`. Set `defaultStyle.font` to a registered font family, as shown above.

---

# Getting started

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/getting-started/

## Choose your runtime

- [Node.js](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/): write a file, return a Buffer from an API, or consume a stream.
- [Browser](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/): download, open, print, or obtain a Blob.

Both runtimes use the same [document definition](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/). Output helpers return Promises. Font loading differs between Node files and browser font containers.

## Before you begin

Use the docs for your installed version (`npm ls pdfmake`). Start with a minimal example before adding custom fonts, remote images or table layouts. For 0.1/0.2 applications, follow the [migration guide](/docs/0.3/migration-from-0.1/).

## JavaScript and TypeScript

This development branch bundles native TypeScript declarations with the library, with separate Node and browser APIs. Install TypeScript without `@types/pdfmake` when using the locally packed branch. The published npm package 0.3.12 still needs its matching community types; the native declarations and preflight API described here are unreleased. The tested compiler is TypeScript 5.9.3.

```sh
npm install pdfmake@0.3.12
npm install --save-dev typescript@~5.9.3
```

Node.js: save this as `document.mts`. Use `NodeNext` so the compiler models actual Node imports. A CommonJS `.cts` file can instead start with `import pdfmake = require("pdfmake")`. Avoid relying on named runtime imports.

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "NodeNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true
  }
}
```

**JavaScript**

```js
import pdfmake from 'pdfmake';
import { strict as assert } from 'node:assert';
pdfmake.addFonts({ Helvetica: { normal: 'Helvetica', bold: 'Helvetica-Bold', italics: 'Helvetica-Oblique', bolditalics: 'Helvetica-BoldOblique' } });
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(name => name.startsWith('Helvetica'));
const definition = { content: [{ table: { body: [['ESM', 'TypeScript'], ['Promise', 'Output']] } }], defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' } };
const buffer = await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).getBuffer();
assert.equal(buffer.subarray(0, 5).toString(), '%PDF-');
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import pdfmake from 'pdfmake';
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from 'pdfmake/interfaces.js';
import { strict as assert } from 'node:assert';

pdfmake.addFonts({ Helvetica: { normal: 'Helvetica', bold: 'Helvetica-Bold', italics: 'Helvetica-Oblique', bolditalics: 'Helvetica-BoldOblique' } });
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(name => name.startsWith('Helvetica'));
const definition: TDocumentDefinitions = { content: [{ table: { body: [['ESM', 'TypeScript'], ['Promise', 'Output']] } }], defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' } };
const buffer: Buffer = await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).getBuffer();
assert.equal(buffer.subarray(0, 5).toString(), '%PDF-');
```

Browser bundlers: import the prebuilt browser entry and register the VFS directly. Use `module: "ESNext"` and `moduleResolution: "Bundler"` in your bundler project; these options require a bundler and are not a configuration for directly running Node output.

**JavaScript**

```js
import pdfmake from 'pdfmake/build/pdfmake.js';
import vfs from 'pdfmake/build/vfs_fonts.js';
pdfmake.addVirtualFileSystem(vfs);
const definition = { content: [{ text: 'TypeScript browser bundler', bold: true }] };
export async function render() {
    return pdfmake.createPdf(definition).getBlob();
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import pdfmake from 'pdfmake/build/pdfmake.js';
import vfs from 'pdfmake/build/vfs_fonts.js';
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from 'pdfmake/interfaces';

pdfmake.addVirtualFileSystem(vfs);
const definition = { content: [{ text: 'TypeScript browser bundler', bold: true }] } satisfies TDocumentDefinitions;
export async function render(): Promise<Blob> {
  return pdfmake.createPdf(definition).getBlob();
}
```

Types provide completion and compile-time checks. They do not validate external JSON or guarantee a successful layout. The bundled declarations distinguish Node `write` from browser `getBlob`, `download`, `open` and `print`. Use explicit browser imports for bundlers. The playground and inline examples check TypeScript locally before rendering. See [document validation](/docs/0.3/guides/errors/) for runtime checks.

---

# Browser quickstart

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/

## Install and copy the browser assets

```sh
npm install pdfmake@0.3.12
```

Copy `node_modules/pdfmake/build/pdfmake.min.js` and `node_modules/pdfmake/build/vfs_fonts.js` next to this HTML file. Serve the directory with your local development server.

## Generate a PDF

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head><meta charset="utf-8"><title>My first PDF</title></head>
<body>
  <button id="download" type="button">Download PDF</button>
  <p id="status" role="status"></p>
  <script src="./pdfmake.min.js"></script>
  <script src="./vfs_fonts.js"></script>
  <script>
    document.querySelector('#download').addEventListener('click', async () => {
      try {
        await pdfMake.createPdf({ content: ['Hello from the browser!'] }).download('hello.pdf');
        document.querySelector('#status').textContent = 'PDF prepared';
      } catch (error) {
        document.querySelector('#status').textContent = 'PDF generation failed';
        console.error(error);
      }
    });
  </script>
</body>
</html>
```

Load the engine **before** its font bundle. `vfs_fonts.js` supplies the default Roboto font files. You do not need a server-side rendering API for this example. `download()` resolving means the download has been initiated; it does not confirm a user saved the file.

## Use a bundler

**JavaScript**

```js
import pdfMake from 'pdfmake/build/pdfmake';
import pdfFonts from 'pdfmake/build/vfs_fonts';

pdfMake.addVirtualFileSystem(pdfFonts);
await pdfMake.createPdf({ content: ['Bundled application'] }).download('document.pdf');
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import pdfMake from 'pdfmake/build/pdfmake';
import pdfFonts from 'pdfmake/build/vfs_fonts';

pdfMake.addVirtualFileSystem(pdfFonts);
await pdfMake.createPdf({ content: ['Bundled application'] }).download('document.pdf');
```

This code runs inside your application's module or async event handler. Keep imports out of server-only execution when using SSR frameworks. For TypeScript, use declarations compatible with your installed pdfmake version; types do not make an older runtime support the 0.3 API.

## Open and print

Call `open()` or `print()` from a user gesture to avoid popup blocking. When fetching data first, open a window synchronously and pass it to the output method afterward. See [browser methods](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/methods/).

## Next steps

[Custom fonts](/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/) · [Browser methods](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/methods/) · [Troubleshooting](/docs/0.3/guides/troubleshooting/)

# Browser output methods

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/methods/

## Create a document

After [loading the engine and fonts](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/):

**JavaScript**

```js
const output = pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition, options);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const output = pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition, options);
```

The optional second argument contains [rendering options](/docs/0.3/options/). `createPdf` returns an output wrapper immediately. Output helpers return Promises; handle their rejection.

## Choose an output

| Method | Resolves to | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `download(filename?)` | `undefined` | Initiate a download; filename defaults to `file.pdf` |
| `open(window?)` | `undefined` | Navigate a new or supplied window to the generated PDF |
| `print(window?)` | `undefined` | Open a PDF carrying a print action; viewer behavior varies |
| `getBlob()` | `Blob` | Binary data with MIME type `application/pdf` |
| `getBuffer()` | Buffer-compatible bytes | Raw PDF bytes |
| `getBase64()` | `string` | Base64-encoded PDF |
| `getDataUrl()` | `string` | Base64 data URL |
| `getStream()` | PDFKit stream | Low-level output; usually prefer Blob or bytes |

**JavaScript**

```js
try {
  await pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition).download('report.pdf');
} catch (error) {
  console.error('PDF generation failed', error);
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
try {
  await pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition).download('report.pdf');
} catch (error) {
  console.error('PDF generation failed', error);
}
```

A resolved download Promise does not confirm that the user saved the file. Printing depends on the browser and PDF viewer; do not rely on silent printing.

## Open after asynchronous work

Open the window directly inside a user click handler, before awaiting data. Otherwise popup blockers may reject it.

**JavaScript**

```js
async function openReport() {
  const win = window.open('', '_blank');
  if (!win) throw new Error('Allow popups to open the PDF');
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/report-data');
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Could not load report data');
    const data = await response.json();
    const definition = { content: [String(data.title)] };
    await pdfMake.createPdf(definition).open(win);
  } catch (error) {
    win.close();
    throw error;
  }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
async function openReport() {
  const win = window.open('', '_blank');
  if (!win) throw new Error('Allow popups to open the PDF');
  try {
    const response = await fetch('/report-data');
    if (!response.ok) throw new Error('Could not load report data');
    const data = await response.json();
    const definition = { content: [String(data.title)] };
    await pdfMake.createPdf(definition).open(win);
  } catch (error) {
    win.close();
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Call `openReport` from your application's click handler and handle its rejected Promise. For printing, replace `.open(win)` with `.print(win)`. Passing `window` navigates the current tab. Set the document's [metadata title](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/document-medatadata/) to label the PDF; viewer filenames and titles remain browser-dependent.

## Manage Blob URLs

**JavaScript**

```js
const blob = await pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition).getBlob();
const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
document.querySelector('#preview').src = url;
// Revoke url when replacing the preview or removing it, after it is no longer needed.
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const blob = await pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition).getBlob();
const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
document.querySelector('#preview').src = url;
// Revoke url when replacing the preview or removing it, after it is no longer needed.
```

Keep the URL alive while the viewer uses it. Call `URL.revokeObjectURL(url)` during cleanup. Use a fresh output wrapper for each render. Avoid mixing manual stream consumption with buffer or Blob helpers on the same output.

## URL access policy

Since **0.3.6**, `setUrlAccessPolicy(callback)` accepts a synchronous boolean callback. It is not a complete network sandbox, and browser redirects may happen before the final URL is checked. See [resource security](/docs/0.3/guides/resource-security/).

# Node.js quickstart

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/

## Install

Use Node.js **20 or later**. Create an application and install pdfmake:

```sh
npm init -y
npm install pdfmake@0.3.12
```

The exact version makes this example reproducible. Check release notes and test before choosing a newer patch.

## Write your first PDF

Save this complete example as `first-pdf.cjs`, then run `node first-pdf.cjs`.

**JavaScript**

```js
// docs-test: node-quickstart
const pdfmake = require('pdfmake');

const fonts = require('pdfmake/standard-fonts/Helvetica');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
const standardNames = new Set(Object.values(fonts.Helvetica));
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(name => standardNames.has(name));

async function main() {
  const definition = {
    defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' },
    content: [
      { text: 'Hello, pdfmake!', fontSize: 24, bold: true },
      'Your first PDF, generated in Node.js.'
    ]
  };
  await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).write('document.pdf');
}

main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";
// docs-test: node-quickstart
import pdfmake from "pdfmake";

const fonts = require('pdfmake/standard-fonts/Helvetica');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
const standardNames = new Set(Object.values(fonts.Helvetica));
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(name => standardNames.has(name));

async function main() {
  const definition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' },
    content: [
      { text: 'Hello, pdfmake!', fontSize: 24, bold: true },
      'Your first PDF, generated in Node.js.'
    ]
  };
  await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).write('document.pdf');
}

main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
```

`write()` resolves when the output file has closed. Handle rejected Promises so failed generation cannot silently produce a successful API response.

Helvetica needs no local font files, so the example denies external URLs and allows only the standard font identifiers through the local policy. The current implementation checks these identifiers even though they are not file paths. Standard fonts have limited character coverage. For multilingual documents, [register suitable font files](/docs/0.3/fonts/) and explicitly allow their resolved paths.

## Return PDF bytes from an API

**JavaScript**

```js
const buffer = await pdfmake.createPdf({
  defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' },
  content: ['API document']
}).getBuffer();

// Adapt these lines to your HTTP framework:
response.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/pdf');
response.setHeader('Content-Disposition', 'attachment; filename="document.pdf"');
response.end(buffer);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const buffer = await pdfmake.createPdf({
  defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' },
  content: ['API document']
}).getBuffer();

// Adapt these lines to your HTTP framework:
response.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/pdf');
response.setHeader('Content-Disposition', 'attachment; filename="document.pdf"');
response.end(buffer);
```

This snippet assumes `pdfmake` is configured as above and `response` is your framework's response object. Validate request data before building a definition. Construct a fresh definition for each request; layout mutates it.

## ESM applications

The Node package exports a configured singleton. In an ESM application use `import pdfmake from 'pdfmake'`; do not instantiate it with `new PdfPrinter(...)` as in older examples. Register fonts and policies once during application startup. Avoid changing singleton configuration per concurrent request.

# Node.js output methods

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/methods/

## Create a document

**JavaScript**

```js
const output = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition, options);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const output = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition, options);
```

`docDefinition` is a [document definition](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/). `options` is an optional [options object](/docs/0.3/options/). `createPdf` returns an output wrapper immediately; generation errors reject the output method's Promise. Invalid argument types can throw synchronously.

## Output helpers

| Method | Resolves to | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `write(filename)` | `undefined` | Write a file and wait for it to close |
| `getBuffer()` | `Buffer` | Return PDF bytes from an API |
| `getBase64()` | `string` | Encode the bytes as base64 |
| `getDataUrl()` | `string` | Prefix base64 with `data:application/pdf;base64,` |
| `getStream()` | PDFKit document stream | Manage a stream directly |

**JavaScript**

```js
try {
  const output = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition);
  const bytes = await output.getBuffer();
  // Send or store bytes here.
} catch (error) {
  // Report generation failure to your caller.
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
try {
  const output = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition);
  const bytes = await output.getBuffer();
  // Send or store bytes here.
} catch (error) {
  // Report generation failure to your caller.
}
```

`getBuffer()` caches its Promise; `getBase64()` and `getDataUrl()` reuse those bytes. Create a new output wrapper for an independent render. Do not combine manual stream consumption with buffer/file helpers on the same wrapper.

## Consume a stream

**JavaScript**

```js
const stream = await pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition).getStream();
stream.on('error', error => { /* Handle generation errors. */ });
destination.on('error', error => { /* Handle destination errors. */ });
stream.pipe(destination);
stream.end();
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const stream = await pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition).getStream();
stream.on('error', error => { /* Handle generation errors. */ });
destination.on('error', error => { /* Handle destination errors. */ });
stream.pipe(destination);
stream.end();
```

`destination` must be a writable stream managed by your application. Attach listeners before calling `end()`. Prefer `write()` for a simple file. Streaming output does not make document layout incremental: pdfmake still lays out the document before returning this stream.

## URL access policy

Available since **0.3.6**. Configure it before creating documents:

**JavaScript**

```js
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(url => {
  const parsed = new URL(url);
  return parsed.protocol === 'https:' && parsed.hostname === 'assets.example.com';
});
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(url => {
  const parsed = new URL(url);
  return parsed.protocol === 'https:' && parsed.hostname === 'assets.example.com';
});
```

The callback must return the boolean `true` **synchronously** to allow a URL. An `async` function returns a Promise and is rejected by the current implementation. An allowlist is only one layer of SSRF protection; use network controls or supply validated bytes when processing untrusted input. See [resource security](/docs/0.3/guides/resource-security/).

## Local file access policy

Available since **0.3.8**. Deny local files when all resources are embedded:

**JavaScript**

```js
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(() => false);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(() => false);
```

For local fonts or images, allow exact resolved paths rather than a string prefix. See the [complete local font setup](/docs/0.3/fonts/). `undefined` clears a configured policy; an omitted policy is not a deny-all policy.

## Engine requirement

The 0.3.12 package declares **Node.js >=20** in `package.json`. The proposed CI matrix covers Node.js 20, 22 and 24 on Linux, Windows and macOS. Compatibility coverage is separate from upstream Node.js security support.

Use a Node.js release that is still maintained for production. Consult the [official Node.js release schedule](https://github.com/nodejs/Release#release-schedule) before choosing a runtime. Test your own fonts, resources and document workload on the exact version you deploy.

# API at a glance

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/api-reference/

## Configure once, render many

Both entry points expose a singleton. Configure fonts, policies and layouts at application startup. Do not replace shared configuration while concurrent requests are rendering.

| Method | Runtime | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addFonts(fonts)` | Both | Merge font families; a supplied family replaces the previous family mapping |
| `setFonts(fonts)` | Both | Replace the whole font map |
| `clearFonts()` | Both | Clear registered fonts |
| `addTableLayouts(layouts)` | Both | Merge named layout functions |
| `setTableLayouts(layouts)` | Both | Replace named layouts |
| `clearTableLayouts()` | Both | Clear custom layouts |
| `setProgressCallback(callback)` | Both | Receive rendering progress; not a page-layout profiler |
| `setUrlAccessPolicy(callback)` | Both, since 0.3.6 | Allow resource URLs only when callback returns `true` synchronously |
| `setLocalAccessPolicy(callback)` | Node, since 0.3.8 | Allow local resources only when callback returns `true` synchronously |
| `addVirtualFileSystem(vfs)` | Browser | Add base64 font/resource data to the virtual filesystem |
| `addFontContainer(container)` | Browser | Register a packaged font container |

## Render

`createPdf(docDefinition, options?)` accepts objects and returns an output wrapper. Use [document fields](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/) in the first argument and [render options](/docs/0.3/options/) in the second.

| Output | Node | Browser |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `getBuffer()`, `getBase64()`, `getDataUrl()`, `getStream()` | Yes | Yes |
| `write(filename)` | Yes | No |
| `download(filename?)`, `open(window?)`, `print(window?)`, `getBlob()` | No | Yes |

All output helpers return Promises. Always handle rejection. The `createPdf` wrapper itself is not a Promise. See [Node methods](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/methods/) and [browser methods](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/methods/) for lifecycle details.

---

# Contributing and source architecture

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/contributing/

## Source map

The library and this site have separate repositories:

- [bpampuch/pdfmake](https://github.com/bpampuch/pdfmake): engine, bundles, tests and examples.
- [pdfmake/docs](https://github.com/pdfmake/docs): this versioned developer site and documentation tools.

The library's Node entry is `src/index.js`; common configuration lives in `src/base.js`. Browser integration lives in `src/browser-extensions/`. `Printer` prepares resources and creates PDFKit output. `DocPreprocessor` normalizes nodes, `DocMeasure` and `TextInlines` measure them, `LayoutBuilder` and `TableProcessor` paginate them, and `Renderer` writes PDFKit drawing instructions.

## Validate engine changes

```sh
npm ci
npm test
npm run build:examples
npm run test:package
```

`npm test` builds generated Node and browser artifacts, then runs Mocha and ESLint. Unit tests import compiled `js/`, so rebuild after editing `src/`. Do not edit `js/` or `build/` directly. The new package smoke test installs the actual tarball in a temporary consumer with production dependencies, then exercises Node output and both browser bundles. It does not replace testing in real browsers.

Preserve text, font metrics, style inheritance and pagination when optimizing. Add an edge-case regression and, when possible, a comparison with the previous behavior. Keep a performance benchmark separate from correctness gates.

## Validate documentation changes

Use Node >=24.11 and Hugo **0.168.0**. From this repository:

```sh
npm ci
npm run docs:generate
npm test
npm run build
npm run dev
```

Open the address printed by Hugo. Generation produces the website search index, Markdown exports and MCP corpus from `content/`. Tests check metadata, examples and MCP behavior. The build verifies generated internal links and fragment targets. Commit regenerated outputs alongside source edits so clients can use the corpus without installing Hugo.

## Releases

The library retains its upstream GitHub Release trigger. The proposed workflow checks tag/version agreement, builds, tests, generates examples, tests a packed consumer, then publishes that same tarball with provenance. No registry publication happens when running local tests.

The docs workflow builds and uploads a review artifact on pushes and pull requests; it does not overwrite the versioned production site. That site's existing multi-version publishing arrangement must be coordinated with maintainers before changing deployment.

---

# Errors and diagnostics

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/errors/

## First identify the failing stage

An invalid definition should fail rather than silently omit content. The useful
question is where it failed and how that error reaches your application.

| Stage | Typical failure | Where to fix it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript parsing | Missing comma, quote or closing brace | Source editor; the library has not been called yet |
| Definition execution | `ReferenceError` or a failing callback | Application code constructing the definition |
| Document structure | Misspelled node type, invalid table rows or list | The reported definition path |
| Resource loading | Missing font, rejected URL, unreadable image | Font/resource registration and access policies |
| Layout/rendering | Content too large, invalid dimensions or callback failure | The smallest reproducing definition |
| Output | Closed stream, write permissions or destination failure | Buffer/stream/file error handling |

## Always await the output

**JavaScript**

```js
async function generateReport(pdfmake, definition) {
  try {
    return await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).getBuffer();
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('PDF generation failed', {
      message: error.message,
      code: error.code,
      phase: error.phase,
      path: error.path
    });
    throw error;
  }
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
async function generateReport(pdfmake, definition) {
  try {
    return await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).getBuffer();
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('PDF generation failed', {
      message: error.message,
      code: error.code,
      phase: error.phase,
      path: error.path
    });
    throw error;
  }
}
```

Return an error to the API caller or display `error.message` in the UI. Do not
respond with an empty PDF or report success after swallowing the rejection.
Avoid logging document contents or private resource credentials.

## Read a document path

The local library improvement branch adds `PDFMAKE_INVALID_DOCUMENT` diagnostics
with `phase: 'preprocess'` and a `path` property. For example:

```text
Unrecognized document structure: ...
Document path: content[0].columns[0].ul[1]
```

This points to the second list item in the first column of the first body node.
Check for a typo such as `{ txt: 'Hello' }` instead of `{ text: 'Hello' }`.
Malformed table rows identify the row and expected number of cells. Empty tables
explain that `table.body` needs nonempty row arrays. Retain `{}` placeholders for
spanned cells. Existing error text is retained; callers should use the diagnostic
fields when present instead of parsing message strings.

These structured diagnostics are **new in the local improvement branch**; the
published 0.3.12 package does not yet contain them. Generic errors still have a
message. The branch also rejects prematurely closed buffer streams instead of
leaving their Promise pending.

## Syntax errors in the playground

The editor parses the definition before executing it, marks the faulty location,
and displays a line and column. **Go to error in editor** focuses the location.
Undo/redo and the error panel let you correct a mistake without losing work.
With live preview, the last successful PDF stays visible during edits and failures,
but its download is disabled when it no longer matches the current source.

## Reduce difficult failures

Keep the same fonts and runtime. Replace the body with a single paragraph, then
add blocks back until the issue returns. For tables, check row lengths and spans
before adjusting widths. For resource failures, start with a known local font and
embedded image. See [troubleshooting](/docs/0.3/guides/troubleshooting/) for more symptoms.

## Validate the complete definition before rendering

The local, unreleased API `validateDocument(input, options)` checks all declared document properties and collects multiple errors with paths. It also checks tables, spans, references, numeric ranges and circular structures. It does not mutate input, execute callbacks or access resources. Unknown properties are warnings by default; use `strict: true` to treat them as errors.

**JavaScript**

```js
const input = { content: [{ text: 'Report', fontSize: 'large' }] };
const report = pdfMake.validateDocument(input, { strict: true });
for (const issue of report.errors) {
  console.error(issue.path, issue.code, issue.message);
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const input = { content: [{ text: 'Report', fontSize: 'large' }] };
const report = pdfMake.validateDocument(input, { strict: true });
for (const issue of report.errors) {
  console.error(issue.path, issue.code, issue.message);
}
```

The result contains `valid`, `errors`, `warnings`, `deferred` and `truncated`. Each diagnostic includes `path`, `code`, `severity` and `message`. Defaults: 100 diagnostics, 100 nesting levels and 50,000 inspected values. An exhausted limit never reports success. Callback results, resource availability/decoding and final layout remain render-time checks. JavaScript syntax must already parse before this object API can run.

Pass `{ validation: true }` as the second argument to `createPdf` to reject invalid definitions before resource loading. An invalid document throws a `DocumentValidationError` with `code: "PDFMAKE_VALIDATION_ERROR"`, `phase: "validation"` and a `diagnostics` array. Existing calls remain compatible; automatic preflight is opt-in. The local playground runs this check automatically when using the improved library.

---

# Invoice recipe

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/invoice/

## Run the example

Install `pdfmake@0.3.12`, save this as `invoice.cjs`, and run `node invoice.cjs`. It uses standard Helvetica with ASCII content to avoid external resources. Use embedded fonts for wider language coverage.

**JavaScript**

```js
// docs-test: invoice
const pdfmake = require('pdfmake');
const fonts = require('pdfmake/standard-fonts/Helvetica');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
const standardNames = new Set(Object.values(fonts.Helvetica));
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(name => standardNames.has(name));

async function main() {
  const items = [
    { description: 'Design services', quantity: 2, unitPriceCents: 12500 },
    { description: 'Document review', quantity: 1, unitPriceCents: 7500 }
  ];
  const money = cents => (cents / 100).toFixed(2) + ' EUR';
  const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.quantity * item.unitPriceCents, 0);
  const definition = {
    defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica', fontSize: 10 },
    pageMargins: [40, 50, 40, 50],
    info: { title: 'Invoice INV-001', author: 'Example Studio' },
    footer: (page, pages) => ({ text: `Page ${page} of ${pages}`, alignment: 'center', fontSize: 9 }),
    content: [
      { text: 'INVOICE', style: 'title' },
      { columns: ['Example Studio', { text: 'INV-001', alignment: 'right' }], margin: [0, 0, 0, 20] },
      { layout: 'lightHorizontalLines', table: {
        headerRows: 1,
        widths: ['*', 'auto', 'auto', 'auto'],
        body: [
          ['Description', 'Qty', 'Unit price', 'Amount'].map(text => ({ text, bold: true })),
          ...items.map(item => [item.description, item.quantity, money(item.unitPriceCents),
            { text: money(item.quantity * item.unitPriceCents), alignment: 'right' }])
        ]
      } },
      { text: 'Total: ' + money(total), alignment: 'right', bold: true, margin: [0, 16, 0, 0] }
    ],
    styles: { title: { fontSize: 28, bold: true, margin: [0, 0, 0, 16] } }
  };
  await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).write('invoice.pdf');
}

main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";
// docs-test: invoice
import pdfmake from "pdfmake";
const fonts = require('pdfmake/standard-fonts/Helvetica');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
const standardNames = new Set(Object.values(fonts.Helvetica));
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(name => standardNames.has(name));

async function main() {
  const items = [
    { description: 'Design services', quantity: 2, unitPriceCents: 12500 },
    { description: 'Document review', quantity: 1, unitPriceCents: 7500 }
  ];
  const money = (cents: number) => (cents / 100).toFixed(2) + ' EUR';
  const total = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.quantity * item.unitPriceCents, 0);
  const definition: TDocumentDefinitions = {
    defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica', fontSize: 10 },
    pageMargins: [40, 50, 40, 50],
    info: { title: 'Invoice INV-001', author: 'Example Studio' },
    footer: (page, pages) => ({ text: `Page ${page} of ${pages}`, alignment: 'center', fontSize: 9 }),
    content: [
      { text: 'INVOICE', style: 'title' },
      { columns: ['Example Studio', { text: 'INV-001', alignment: 'right' }], margin: [0, 0, 0, 20] },
      { layout: 'lightHorizontalLines', table: {
        headerRows: 1,
        widths: ['*', 'auto', 'auto', 'auto'],
        body: [
          ['Description', 'Qty', 'Unit price', 'Amount'].map(text => ({ text, bold: true })),
          ...items.map(item => [item.description, item.quantity, money(item.unitPriceCents),
            { text: money(item.quantity * item.unitPriceCents), alignment: 'right' }])
        ]
      } },
      { text: 'Total: ' + money(total), alignment: 'right', bold: true, margin: [0, 16, 0, 0] }
    ],
    styles: { title: { fontSize: 28, bold: true, margin: [0, 0, 0, 16] } }
  };
  await pdfmake.createPdf(definition).write('invoice.pdf');
}

main().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode = 1; });
```

## Adapt it to your application

This is a layout example, not a tax or accounting implementation. Validate quantities and prices before generating the definition. Amounts use integer cents to avoid decimal accumulation in this example; apply your domain's rounding rules separately. For an HTTP response, replace `write()` with `getBuffer()` as shown in the [Node.js quickstart](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/).

`headerRows: 1` repeats the table header when rows continue onto a new page. Keep each row the same length as `widths`. Make a fresh definition for every invoice.

# LLM and MCP integration

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/llm-and-mcp/

## Use documentation without MCP

Every page is available as generated Markdown. The same source produces:

- [llms.txt](/docs/0.3/llms.txt): page index with descriptions and Markdown links.
- [llms-full.txt](/docs/0.3/llms-full.txt): the complete versioned Markdown corpus.
- [docs-index.json](/docs/0.3/docs-index.json): page IDs, titles, descriptions, source URLs and full Markdown.

These are discovery aids, not a search-engine or model-indexing guarantee. Keep the installed library version in your prompt. Ask the model to cite the page and use Promise output methods. The library's `AGENTS.md` explains its source pipeline and test commands to coding agents.

## Run the local MCP server

Clone the documentation repository, install its dependencies, generate the corpus and start the server:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/pdfmake/docs.git
cd docs
npm ci
npm run docs:generate
node mcp/server.mjs
```

This server is part of the local improvement branch until accepted upstream. Start it through your MCP client's stdio configuration, using absolute paths:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "pdfmake-docs": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/absolute/path/to/docs/mcp/server.mjs"]
    }
  }
}
```

Replace the example path with your clone's path. On Windows JSON paths must use `/` or escaped `\\`. Client configuration locations vary. The server writes protocol messages to stdout and errors to stderr. It does not require an API key, model account or network connection after dependency installation.

## Tools and resources

| Capability | Input | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `search_docs` | `query`, optional `limit` (1–10), optional `language` | Ranked pages with exact IDs, language, version, source URLs and excerpts |
| `get_doc` | Exact `id` from search | Complete Markdown page |
| MCP resources | `pdfmake://docs/0.3/<id>` | The same versioned Markdown page |

The server can only read its bundled documentation corpus. It cannot render PDFs, evaluate code, read caller-selected filesystem paths or browse remote URLs. Re-run generation and restart it after editing documentation.

`language` accepts `en` (default), `de`, `fr`, `es` and `pt-br`. Every supported language contains the same complete set of documentation pages. Search never silently mixes languages. A translated ID such as `de/learn/first-pdf` can be read with `get_doc` or the resource `pdfmake://docs/0.3/de/learn/first-pdf`. Each language also has its own discovery files, for example `/docs/0.3/de/llms.txt` and `/docs/0.3/de/llms-full.txt`.

## Suggested prompt

> I use pdfmake 0.3.x in Node.js. Search the matching documentation before generating code. Use the Node singleton API, register fonts, configure synchronous resource policies, await output, and cite the page IDs used. Build a fresh document definition per request.

---

# Performance and memory

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/performance/

## Measure your workload

Benchmark representative documents with the same Node version, fonts and input data. Record median and tail latency, peak memory, page count and output size. Separate cold startup/font loading from repeated renders. Compare table-heavy, long-text and image-heavy documents separately.

**JavaScript**

```js
const start = performance.now();
const bytes = await pdfmake.createPdf(makeFreshDefinition()).getBuffer();
console.log({ milliseconds: performance.now() - start, bytes: bytes.length });
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const start = performance.now();
const bytes = await pdfmake.createPdf(makeFreshDefinition()).getBuffer();
console.log({ milliseconds: performance.now() - start, bytes: bytes.length });
```

`makeFreshDefinition()` is your own factory. Do not reuse a definition already mutated by layout. Verify text, page counts and representative rendered pages as well as speed.

## Reduce avoidable work

- Put repeated images in the `images` dictionary and reference them by key. Resize large source images before embedding them; display dimensions do not reduce the original payload.
- Prefer fixed widths when your layout permits them. Content-driven `auto` widths require text measurement; benchmark before redesigning tables.
- Register fonts once. In browser applications, ship only needed font families and variants.
- Keep `fontLayoutCache` enabled unless a measured compatibility problem requires disabling it. See [render options](/docs/0.3/options/).
- Avoid base64 when your API can return binary PDF bytes. Base64 represents each three bytes with four characters and also allocates a string.
- Use `write()` or direct stream consumption to avoid the additional concatenated Buffer produced by `getBuffer()` when you only need a file or stream. Layout still occurs before output consumption.

## Control concurrency

More simultaneous PDF jobs can increase memory use and event-loop delay. Bound concurrent renders and load-test throughput rather than only measuring one request. Use worker threads or separate processes when blocking work affects API responsiveness. Keep mutable singleton configuration out of per-request code.

## Library development benchmark

The library improvement branch includes `npm run benchmark:text` after `npm run build:node`. It compares text-array flattening with the previous algorithm using deterministic mixed input and verifies equivalent results. The optimized loop avoids repeated prefix copying. Its speedup measures that helper only; it is not a claim about total PDF generation time.

Timing thresholds are deliberately excluded from CI because shared runners are noisy. Use correctness tests as gates and retain benchmark results with environment details for review.

---

# Playground guide

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/playground/

## Learn by editing

Open the [playground](/docs/0.3/playground/), choose an example and edit the definition
in the left panel. The right panel shows a real PDF rendered through PDF.js.
With **Live preview** enabled, the PDF updates automatically after editing. Select **Run** or press **Ctrl/Command + Enter** for an immediate update.

The CodeMirror 6 editor includes syntax highlighting, line numbers, bracket matching, indentation, Undo/Redo buttons, persistent undo history and syntax diagnostics with line and column. Go to error focuses the offending source location. It also provides completions. Use **Ctrl + Space** to request completions. Suggested field names
are hints; the document reference defines the valid context, type and values.

## Examples

| Example | Explore |
| --- | --- |
| [First document](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=welcome) | Text, spacing and font styles |
| [Invoice](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=invoice) | A table, totals and a page-number footer |
| [Tables](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=tables) | Repeating headers across multiple pages |
| [Text styles](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=styles) | Named styles and inline overrides |
| [Columns](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=columns) | Side-by-side blocks and stacks |
| [Spans](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=spans) | Row and column spans with placeholders |
| [Pages](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=pages) | Page breaks, headers and footers |
| [Vectors](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=vectors) | Embedded SVG and QR codes |
| [Images](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=images) | Embedded PNG data reused by name |
| [Lists](/docs/0.3/playground/?example=lists) | Numbered lists, bullets and links |

An `example` URL parameter selects a known example; it does not accept JavaScript.
Live preview also updates restored workspaces, saved documents and imported files.
Turn **Live preview** off before importing code you want to inspect first.

## Preview and output

Use the arrow buttons to change pages and the zoom menu to change scale. **Page
text** exposes text extracted from the current PDF page for inspection and assistive
technology. **Open PDF** opens the generated file separately; **Download PDF** saves
the same PDF bytes. The footer shows generation time and output size. Generation
time excludes PDF.js preview rendering.

Live preview waits 650 ms after the last edit, then renders in a fresh worker. The old PDF stays visible until the next page has finished rendering off screen; the canvas is then replaced in one step. The selected PDF page and zoom are retained where possible. Downloads are disabled while the visible PDF does not match the current code. Errors keep the last successful preview instead of replacing it with a blank panel.

## Keep your work

**Export code** downloads the current definition as JavaScript. **Import .js** reads
a local file. Files are limited to 500 KB. Disable **Live preview** before importing
code you want to review before running it. Resetting or changing examples asks before replacing edits.

**The current workspace is autosaved locally**, including the definition, editor selection, undo history, example, page and zoom settings. Reloading restores the editor, its Undo/Redo history and the Live preview preference. If Live preview is enabled, the restored PDF renders automatically and subsequent edits update it without pressing Run. If disabled, rendering stays manual, including after a reload.

Give the document a name and choose **Save document** to keep a separate local document. Choosing a new name creates another saved document; saving under the same selected name updates it. The saved-documents menu restores a document and its history. Delete removes that named copy while retaining the current editor contents. Up to 30 named documents can be kept. Browser storage quotas still apply.

**Save draft locally** remains a separate quick snapshot with Restore/Clear controls. **Clear workspace autosave** removes the current autosave and pauses it until you type again. Named documents and quick drafts are separate. If browser storage is disabled or full, the editor still works and code export remains available. No source or PDF is uploaded by this application.

## Rendering boundaries

Each render starts a fresh browser worker. **Cancel** terminates it, including a
blocked JavaScript loop. A ten-second limit stops unexpectedly expensive work.
Simplify large documents or test them in a controlled application when they exceed
the playground limit. The PDF API denies remote URL resources here; use embedded
images and the supplied Roboto fonts.

Custom JavaScript is trusted user code, not a security sandbox. Do not run code from
an unknown source. A worker protects the UI from blocking but is not an isolation
boundary for hostile code. See [resource security](/docs/0.3/guides/resource-security/)
for production API guidance.

## Run the standalone development tool

From a built pdfmake library checkout, run `npm run playground`. This serves the
same UI with that checkout's engine at `http://127.0.0.1:1234/playground/`. It needs
Node >=22.13 for its separate tooling. The published library's runtime requirement
remains Node >=20. The docs site can also preview a local engine using
`PDFMAKE_SOURCE`; see the documentation repository README.

---

# Resource security

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/resource-security/

## Treat definitions as application code

A definition can contain callback functions for headers, footers, table layouts and page breaks. Never evaluate JavaScript submitted by an untrusted caller. Accept validated application data and construct definitions yourself. Limit input size, nesting, table dimensions and image size before rendering.

## Deny resources you do not need

If all resources are supplied as in-memory data, deny string-based resource paths:

**JavaScript**

```js
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(() => false);
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(() => false);
pdfmake.setLocalAccessPolicy(() => false);
```

The current implementation also passes standard font identifiers (for example `Helvetica-Bold`) through the local policy. Allow the exact registered identifiers when using standard fonts; the [Node quickstart](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/) shows this setup.

URL policies require **0.3.6+** and local policies **0.3.8+**. Configure them before accepting work. An unset policy permits resource loading; it does not mean deny-all.

## Use synchronous policies

The implementation checks `callback(value) === true`. Do not use `async` callbacks, DNS lookups or promises inside these policies. Prefetch approved resources in your application if validation requires asynchronous work, then pass embedded data or an application-owned file.

**JavaScript**

```js
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(value => {
  const url = new URL(value);
  return url.protocol === 'https:' && url.hostname === 'assets.example.com' && !url.username && !url.password;
});
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
pdfmake.setUrlAccessPolicy(value => {
  const url = new URL(value);
  return url.protocol === 'https:' && url.hostname === 'assets.example.com' && !url.username && !url.password;
});
```

This hostname example is not complete SSRF protection. DNS changes, redirects, internal address ranges and deployment network permissions also matter. Apply outbound network controls. On Node.js the resolver checks manual redirect hops. Browsers may follow redirects before the final URL policy check; browser policies cannot enforce control of every network hop.

## Local files

Allow exact resolved application-owned paths. See [font configuration](/docs/0.3/fonts/) for a working allowlist. Avoid `startsWith('fonts/')`, which does not resolve traversal or filesystem aliases. Protect approved files from replacement and account for symlinks. Do not let a caller select arbitrary server paths.

## Bound the job

Layout and font work can consume CPU and memory before an output stream is available. Use bounded queues and isolated workers when serving large or untrusted documents. A Promise timeout alone does not interrupt synchronous layout. Add process-level limits if you require hard cancellation.

## PDF encryption is separate

[Passwords and PDF permissions](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/security/) affect the produced document. They do not secure your server's network, filesystem or callback execution.

---

# Troubleshooting

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/guides/troubleshooting/

## Start with version and runtime

Run `npm ls pdfmake` and compare your import to the appropriate quickstart. A browser bundle and the Node entry expose different output helpers. Version 0.1/0.2 examples using `new PdfPrinter(...)` or callbacks do not describe the 0.3 API.

| Symptom | Check | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Font family or variant is not defined | Family name, bold/italic mapping, default font | Register all used variants and select the family in `defaultStyle` |
| File not found or access denied | Actual resolved font/image path and policy | Use existing application-owned paths and a matching synchronous policy |
| Missing or incorrect glyphs | Selected font's glyph coverage | Embed a font covering the language; test bold and italic too |
| Empty or malformed table | `body`, row lengths and spans | Supply nonempty consistent rows and placeholders for spanned cells |
| `download` is not a function on Node | Imported runtime | Use `write` or `getBuffer` on the Node entry |
| Browser opens no window | User gesture and popup blocker | Open a window directly on click before asynchronous data loading |
| URL is denied despite an allow callback | Callback return type | Return literal boolean `true` synchronously; remove `async` |
| HTTP image request fails | URL, policy, CORS, status and redirects | Check access in the target runtime; browsers enforce CORS |
| File is incomplete or missing | Rejected Promise and writable errors | Await `write()` and handle its rejection before reporting success |
| Output changes after an upgrade | Version, fonts, inputs and defaults | Reproduce with a pinned version and compare extracted text, page counts and rendered pages |

## Reduce the definition

Start with one plain paragraph and known-good fonts. Add your styles, table rows and resources one at a time. Construct a fresh definition per attempt. Keep request and resource errors separate from layout errors.

## Report a useful bug

Include the exact pdfmake and Node/browser versions, operating system, a minimal runnable definition, font setup, expected versus actual behavior and the full relevant stack trace. Remove private content and secrets. For pagination defects include the smallest input that still reproduces the page break.

---

# Start here

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/learn/

## Start with one working document

You do not need to learn the whole document reference first. Follow these three steps:



- [1. Make your first PDF](/docs/0.3/learn/first-pdf/): Understand the definition, load fonts and run one complete example.


- [2. Learn the document model](/docs/0.3/learn/document-model/): Know when to use a paragraph, inline text, a stack, columns or a table.


- [3. Read errors and fix the right thing](/docs/0.3/guides/errors/): Separate JavaScript syntax, document structure, resources and output.



## Which runtime do I need?

| Choose | When | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Node.js](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/) | Your API or background job creates the file | `write()` for files; `getBuffer()` for HTTP responses |
| [Browser](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/) | The user creates the document on their device | `download()`, `open()`, `print()` or `getBlob()` |

The document definition is shared. Font loading and output helpers depend on the runtime.
These pages target **0.3.x**; older examples using `new PdfPrinter(...)` and callback
output belong to [0.1/0.2](/docs/0.3/migration-from-0.1/).

## Learn by seeing the result

Examples in this learning path show the exact JavaScript definition beside a real
generated PDF. Open them in the playground to edit them. Their complete source is
also included in the [Markdown corpus](/docs/0.3/llms-full.txt), including the code
otherwise generated by the interactive example components.

---

# The document model

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/learn/document-model/

## Start from content

`content` describes the body of the PDF. A plain string is a paragraph. A content
array is a vertical sequence of blocks. An object describes a node with additional
properties. pdfmake calculates positions; you usually do not specify coordinates.

**JavaScript**

```js
const dd = {
  content: [
    'One paragraph.',
    { text: 'Another paragraph.', bold: true },
    { text: ['One paragraph with ', { text: 'an emphasized part', italics: true }] }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

const dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    'One paragraph.',
    { text: 'Another paragraph.', bold: true },
    { text: ['One paragraph with ', { text: 'an emphasized part', italics: true }] }
  ]
};
```

The nested `text` array creates **inline runs in the same paragraph**. A `content`
array or `stack` creates **separate blocks**. This distinction explains many
surprising line breaks when you first build definitions.

## Choose a container

| Need | Node | Common mistake |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Several paragraphs sharing a style | `{ stack: [...] }` | Trying to assign style properties directly to an array |
| Independent blocks side by side | `{ columns: [...] }` | Expecting rows to line up as in a table |
| Aligned rows and cells | `{ table: { body: [...] } }` | Omitting placeholder cells after `colSpan` or `rowSpan` |
| Bullet or numbered items | `{ ul: [...] }` or `{ ol: [...] }` | Embedding a string where an item array is expected |
| Mixed styles within one line | `{ text: [...] }` | Using a stack, which creates separate blocks |



### Runnable example: 05 · Columns & stacks

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = {
  content: [
    { text: 'Two perspectives', fontSize: 26, bold: true, margin: [0, 0, 0, 20] },
    { columnGap: 24, columns: [
      { width: '*', stack: [{ text: 'The essentials', bold: true }, 'This column takes an equal share of the available width.', { ul: ['Text', 'Lists', 'Nested blocks'] }] },
      { width: '*', stack: [{ text: 'The details', bold: true }, 'Use fixed widths, auto widths or star widths to describe your layout.'] }
    ] }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    { text: 'Two perspectives', fontSize: 26, bold: true, margin: [0, 0, 0, 20] },
    { columnGap: 24, columns: [
      { width: '*', stack: [{ text: 'The essentials', bold: true }, 'This column takes an equal share of the available width.', { ul: ['Text', 'Lists', 'Nested blocks'] }] },
      { width: '*', stack: [{ text: 'The details', bold: true }, 'Use fixed widths, auto widths or star widths to describe your layout.'] }
    ] }
  ]
};
```

[See the rendered PDF and edit this example](https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/playground/?example=columns)



## Put settings at the right level

| Level | Examples | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application configuration | `addFonts`, `addTableLayouts`, resource policies | Register reusable resources before jobs start |
| Document definition | `content`, `styles`, `defaultStyle`, `pageMargins`, `footer` | Describe one PDF |
| Individual node | `text`, `fontSize`, `bold`, `margin`, `pageBreak` | Describe one piece of content |
| Second `createPdf` argument | `fontLayoutCache`, `bufferPages` | Adjust engine options |

Register shared fonts and policies once in a Node service. Build a fresh definition
for every job: layout mutates nodes with measurements and positions. Avoid modifying
the shared pdfmake singleton's configuration during concurrent requests.

## Learn the units and widths

Dimensions use points. A four-value margin is `[left, top, right, bottom]`.
A width number is a fixed point width; `'auto'` follows content; `'*'` shares
remaining space with other star columns. Use fixed or star widths first, then
introduce content-driven sizing when it solves a real layout need.

## Continue with the reference

[Styling](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/styling/) · [Tables](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/tables/)
· [Images](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/images/) · [Page layout](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/page/)
