# Your first PDF

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/learn/first-pdf/

## 1. Understand the two ingredients

pdfmake needs an **engine with fonts** and a **document definition**. The definition
is a JavaScript object describing what to print. It is not HTML and does not draw
anything until you pass it to `createPdf` and request an output.

For your first attempt, use the example below in the browser. It already has the
engine and Roboto font configured. Then use the runtime setup in step 3.

## 2. Look at a complete definition

The result below is generated from exactly this code. Three `content` entries
become three vertical blocks. Text wraps automatically; margins and font sizes
are measured in PDF points (72 points = 1 inch).



### Runnable example: 01 · First document

**JavaScript**

```js
// Define a fresh document in dd. Ctrl/⌘ + Enter to run.
var dd = {
  content: [
    { text: 'Make something clear.', fontSize: 30, bold: true, color: '#08786b', margin: [0, 0, 0, 16] },
    'A paragraph, a table, a report. Start here and make it yours.',
    { text: 'Built with pdfmake', italics: true, color: '#667d73', margin: [0, 20, 0, 0] }
  ]
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

// Define a fresh document in dd. Ctrl/⌘ + Enter to run.
var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = {
  content: [
    { text: 'Make something clear.', fontSize: 30, bold: true, color: '#08786b', margin: [0, 0, 0, 16] },
    'A paragraph, a table, a report. Start here and make it yours.',
    { text: 'Built with pdfmake', italics: true, color: '#667d73', margin: [0, 20, 0, 0] }
  ]
};
```

[See the rendered PDF and edit this example](https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/playground/?example=welcome)



Change the heading or font size in the playground. With **Live preview** enabled,
the next PDF appears after you pause typing. You can undo changes, save named
documents in your browser, or export a JavaScript file.

## 3. Configure your own application

Choose **one** setup. Do not combine the Node entry with browser-only output methods.

| Runtime | Setup | Why fonts matter |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node.js API | [Complete Node quickstart](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/) | Register real font files or a standard family before rendering |
| Browser application | [Complete browser quickstart](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/) | Load `pdfmake.min.js`, then a font VFS, or register it in your bundler |

The example uses `Roboto`, the browser default. If you use it with the Node
quickstart's standard Helvetica setup, add `defaultStyle: { font: 'Helvetica' }`
to the definition or register Roboto files. Unicode text also needs a font covering
the characters you use; a valid string alone does not supply missing glyphs.

## 4. Request an output and handle errors

In a configured browser application:

**JavaScript**

```js
try {
  await pdfMake.createPdf(dd).download('first-document.pdf');
} catch (error) {
  document.querySelector('#status').textContent = error.message;
}
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
try {
  await pdfMake.createPdf(dd).download('first-document.pdf');
} catch (error) {
  document.querySelector('#status').textContent = error.message;
}
```

Here `dd` is the definition above and `#status` is an element in your application.
For Node.js, use `await pdfmake.createPdf(dd).write('first-document.pdf')` instead.
`createPdf` returns an output wrapper; the output method returns the Promise to
await. Without `await` or `.catch(...)`, a generation failure may never reach your UI.

## 5. Add one concept at a time

Keep the first working document. Add [named styles](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/styling/)
next, then [tables](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/tables/) when you need rows.
Use [the document model](/docs/0.3/learn/document-model/) to choose a node type.
If something fails, [classify the error](/docs/0.3/guides/errors/) before changing fonts,
layout and resources all at once.

---

# Migration from 0.1/0.2

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/migration-from-0.1/

## Upgrade deliberately

Pin the version you are evaluating. Keep representative existing PDFs and the inputs/fonts used to generate them. Compare extracted text, page counts and rendered pages before upgrading production. Byte equality is often unsuitable because PDF metadata and identifiers can vary.

## Replace the Node constructor API

Older Node examples construct `PdfPrinter` and call `createPdfKitDocument`. In 0.3 use the singleton:

**JavaScript**

```js
const pdfmake = require('pdfmake');
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
await pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition).write('document.pdf');
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import pdfmake from "pdfmake";
pdfmake.addFonts(fonts);
await pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition).write('document.pdf');
```

`fonts` must be a valid family map, as shown in the [Node quickstart](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/) and [fonts guide](/docs/0.3/fonts/). Configure policies and layouts during startup, and avoid per-request changes to shared singleton state.

## Await output helpers

Replace callback-based browser output with Promises:

**JavaScript**

```js
const data = await pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition).getBase64();
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const data = await pdfMake.createPdf(docDefinition).getBase64();
```

Handle rejections from output methods. Use [Node methods](/docs/0.3/getting-started/server-side/methods/) or [browser methods](/docs/0.3/getting-started/client-side/methods/) for the runtime you target.

## Regenerate browser font storage

Regenerate custom VFS files and update registration to `addVirtualFileSystem`. Do not assume the shape of an older generated font file matches the current bundle. See [VFS fonts](/docs/0.3/fonts/custom-fonts-client-side/vfs/).

## Update pageBreakBefore

Version 0.1/0.2 passed separate node arrays. Version 0.3 passes a node container:

**JavaScript**

```js
var dd = { content: ['Example document'],
pageBreakBefore: function (currentNode, nodeContainer) {
  return currentNode.headlineLevel === 1 &&
    nodeContainer.getFollowingNodesOnPage().length === 0;
}
};
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
import type { TDocumentDefinitions } from "pdfmake/interfaces";

var dd: TDocumentDefinitions = { content: ['Example document'],
pageBreakBefore: function (currentNode, nodeContainer) {
  return currentNode.headlineLevel === 1 &&
    nodeContainer.getFollowingNodesOnPage().length === 0;
}
};
```

The container also offers `getNodesOnNextPage()` and `getPreviousNodesOnPage()`. This snippet is a property inside a definition, not standalone JavaScript. See [page breaks](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/page/).

## Configure resource access

For **0.3.6+**, configure a synchronous URL access policy; for **0.3.8+**, configure a local file policy. Test both permitted and rejected resources. See [resource security](/docs/0.3/guides/resource-security/).

---

# Rendering options

Version: pdfmake 0.3.x
Language: en
Source: https://pdfmake.github.io/docs/0.3/options/

## Pass options to createPdf

**JavaScript**

```js
const output = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition, {
  fontLayoutCache: true,
  bufferPages: false
});
```

**TypeScript**

```ts
const output = pdfmake.createPdf(docDefinition, {
  fontLayoutCache: true,
  bufferPages: false
});
```

The options object is separate from the [document definition](/docs/0.3/document-definition-object/).

| Option | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fontLayoutCache` | boolean | `true` | Enable PDFKit's font layout cache |
| `bufferPages` | boolean | `false` | Keep PDFKit pages buffered rather than flushing them immediately |

Keep defaults unless your use case requires a change. Page buffering can increase memory use. It does not make pdfmake's own layout lazy or incremental. See [performance](/docs/0.3/guides/performance/) and [PDFKit's page buffering documentation](https://pdfkit.org/docs/getting_started.html).

Fonts, named table layouts and resource policies are configured on the [public API](/docs/0.3/guides/api-reference/). Paper size, margins and content belong in the definition.

---
